title: Armenian Feudal Long Swordsmen (21 pop)
summary: Reach the Feudal Age at 21 population, research Man-at-Arms and then Long Swordsman, and walk into your opponent's base with infantry that normally only exists in the Castle Age.
description:
Armenians can research the Long Swordsman upgrade in the Feudal Age. This build gets you there quickly: a 20 villager Dark Age with a Barracks, the Man-at-Arms upgrade the moment Feudal lands, and the Long Swordsman upgrade right after it. Your Long Swordsmen beat Scouts, Spearmen, Men-at-Arms and towers in melee, and they take down Palisade Walls and Houses quickly.

Mule Carts are the reason the Dark Age is so cheap. A cart costs 15 food and 60 wood instead of the 100 wood of a Lumber Camp, and it counts as a building for the Feudal Age requirement. The starting 200 gold is enough for Loom and both upgrades, so you do not need gold miners before the Feudal Age.

Pick this build on open maps like Arabia when you expect a slower opponent or a Scout opening. If you see an Archery Range, keep reading the tips: you will need Skirmishers next to the infantry.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses, then go to the sheep; send the Scout Cavalry out to find sheep, boar and the opponent's base
First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 3 villagers build a Mule Cart at the closest woodline and chop wood
Villager 10 lures the first boar to the Town Center
Villager 11 builds a House, then a Mill at the berries, and forages there
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries)
Villager 15 lures the second boar when the first one is nearly eaten
Next 2 villagers on boar and sheep
Next 3 villagers go to wood (6 on wood); one of them builds a Barracks near the Mule Cart first
Research Loom while the last villager trains
Click up to the Feudal Age with 20 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
While the age loads, train 2 Militia if you have the food; they become Long Swordsmen later
When sheep run low, 3 sheep villagers drive a second Mule Cart to the gold and mine; the rest start Farms
Feudal Age arrives: research the Man-at-Arms upgrade at the Barracks right away
Next 2 villagers to gold (5 on gold), then new villagers go to Farms
As soon as Man-at-Arms finishes, research Long Swordsman (150 food, 65 gold)
Build a second Barracks with a wood villager and research Double-Bit Axe at the Mule Cart
Train infantry from both Barracks without a break
Walk out with your first 5 or 6 Long Swordsmen and hit the gold or wood line, killing Houses and Palisades on the way

after_feudal: Keep both Barracks working and send the Long Swordsmen at villagers, not at the Town Center. Research Scale Mail Armor at a Blacksmith once you have about eight infantry, and add a third or fourth villager per Barracks on Farms so production does not stop. If the opponent answers with archers, build an Archery Range and add Skirmishers, or switch the Barracks to towers next to their gold the way ColinAoC does. Once the damage is done, click Castle Age: Two-Handed Swordsman is available as soon as you land, and a Fortified Church brings the free Relic.
tips: The Long Swordsman upgrade needs Man-at-Arms first, so queue both at the Barracks back to back.
Armenian Spearmen are available in the Dark Age; if you see early Scouts, train two before you click up.
Move the wood Mule Cart along with your lumberjacks instead of building a new drop site.
Long Swordsmen are slow. Use the Scout Cavalry to find their villagers before you walk across the map.
Your infantry has +2 Line of Sight from the team bonus, so you can see archers coming earlier than usual.
beaten_by: Massed Feudal archers with good micro and a walled base are the biggest problem. Answer with Skirmishers from an Archery Range, Scale Mail Armor and a tower at their gold. A fast castle player who walls perfectly can also outscale you, so do not commit every villager to Farms for infantry if you see no damage; go up to Castle Age instead.

title: Fast Castle into Warrior Priests (25+2)
summary: A fast castle that puts a Fortified Church down the moment Castle Age arrives, takes the free Relic and starts Warrior Priests that heal, carry Relics and fight.
description:
The Fortified Church is Armenian Castle Age power: it costs 200 wood, comes with a free Relic the first time you build one, and trains the Warrior Priest. This build skips Feudal fighting, reaches Castle Age with 26 villagers, and puts the church up before anything else.

Warrior Priests are infantry that heal nearby units and carry Relics. Monks cannot convert them before Atonement, so early Castle Age Monks are easy prey for them, and they can grab the Relics on the map while protecting themselves. ColinAoC plays a tighter 22+2 version that leans on the Market to click Castle sooner; the 25+2 below is more forgiving and still fast because Mule Carts save wood in the Dark Age.

Pick it on Arena and other closed maps, or on open maps when you can wall. On Arabia against a fast Feudal rush you have little army, so palisade your wood and gold before clicking Castle Age.

steps.text: The starting villagers build two Houses; scout for sheep, boar and Relics
First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 3 villagers build a Mule Cart at wood and chop
Villager 10 lures the first boar
Villager 11 builds a House and a Mill at the berries, then forages
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries); lure the second boar with villager 15
Next 2 villagers on boar and sheep; seed Farms with the weakest sheep villagers as the sheep run low
Next 4 villagers to wood (7 on wood); move the Mule Cart or add a second one if the woodline splits
Next 3 villagers drive a Mule Cart to gold and mine (3 on gold)
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age with 24 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, put the remaining sheep villagers on Farms and wall the wood and gold lines
Feudal Age arrives: 2 wood villagers build a Blacksmith and a Market
Next 2 villagers to gold (5 on gold)
Click up to the Castle Age as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold
Research Double-Bit Axe at the Mule Cart and Horse Collar at the Mill while the age loads
New villagers go to gold; when berries run out, move them to Farms
Collect about 200 wood for the church before the age up finishes
Castle Age arrives: 3 or 4 wood villagers build the Fortified Church; the free Relic appears inside
Train Warrior Priests nonstop and send the first ones to the closest Relics

after_feudal: Move the next villagers to gold until you have about ten miners, since Warrior Priests cost 40 food and 50 gold each. Use the first four or five to collect Relics and kill enemy Monks, then group them with a few Skirmishers or Halberdiers depending on what you see. A second Town Center comes next, then Gold Mining and Bow Saw at the Mule Carts. Morley Games plays the all-in version with Scorpions behind the priests; the safer path is to boom behind the church and add Two-Handed Swordsmen as the economy grows.
tips: Park the gold Mule Cart close to the spot where you want the Fortified Church; villagers can hide inside it if you get raided.
Warrior Priests heal, so pull hurt infantry back next to them instead of throwing them away.
Relics are worth more the earlier you take them; send priests out before your opponent's Monks arrive.
Keep the Market: you can sell spare wood for gold when the priests drain your gold income.
beaten_by: A strong Feudal rush before you have walls, and fast Knights in the early Castle Age, are the main dangers. Warrior Priests are slow and lose to Knights in the open, so add Spearmen or Pikemen next to them. Massed archers also beat a priest army; answer with Skirmishers and Composite Bowmen.

title: Aztecs Men-at-Arms into Archers (21 pop)
summary: The standard Aztec opening on Arabia: three Militia from a Dark Age Barracks become Men-at-Arms on arrival in Feudal, with Archers behind them. The bonus gold means only two gold miners are needed early.
description:
This is the regular Men-at-Arms into Archers opening, tuned for the Aztecs. Three things change compared to the generic version. You start with 150 gold instead of 100, which pays for the three Militia and the Man-at-Arms upgrade with only two gold miners in the Dark Age. Your Barracks and Archery Range train 15% faster, so the first units are out and walking sooner. And your villagers carry 3 more resources per trip, so the economy keeps up with the early military spending.

The Men-at-Arms hit the enemy wood line or gold as soon as Feudal Age lands, forcing villagers to fight or hide, while an Archery Range starts Archers at home. F1ReAoE plays it as the first step toward a Castle Age switch into mass Eagle Warriors. Pick it on open maps against most civilizations, especially those that like to boom or go Scouts.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; the Eagle Scout looks for sheep. You start with 150 gold thanks to the Aztec bonus
First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House and the Mill on the berries, then forages
Next 2 villagers on berries (3 on berries)
Villager 15 lures the second boar
Next 2 villagers on boar and sheep
Villager 18 goes to wood (5 on wood)
Villager 19 builds the Barracks as soon as you have 175 wood, then a Mining Camp on gold, and mines
Villager 20 also goes to gold (2 on gold); the extra starting gold covers the rest
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age with 20 villagers plus the Eagle Scout
Queue 3 Militia during the age up and walk them toward the enemy as they come out
During the age up, move 3 sheep villagers to wood and seed Farms as the sheep run out
Feudal Age arrives: research Man-at-Arms right away and send the three to the enemy wood line or gold
Build an Archery Range and start Archers; research Double-Bit Axe
Next 2 villagers go to gold (4 on gold); keep adding gold miners as archer production grows
Once 9 or more villagers are on food, build a Blacksmith and research Fletching
New villagers go onto Farms; add Horse Collar when the farms are running

after_feudal:
Use the Men-at-Arms to hit villagers far from the Town Center and pull back when the villagers fight with Loom. Then bring them home to escort the first archers. Keep adding Farms until you have 15 to 17, as F1ReAoE does, and click Castle Age with around 30 villagers.

In the Castle Age you have two paths. Crossbowman and Bodkin Arrow keep the archer plan going. The more typical Aztec plan is to build a Market and two or three extra Barracks and switch to Eagle Warriors, buying food with spare gold since Eagles cost only 20 food. Add a Monastery for relics, and Skirmishers with Atlatl if the opponent masses archers.
tips: You have 150 gold at the start, which covers 3 Militia (60 gold) and the Man-at-Arms upgrade (40 gold).
The Eagle Scout is slower than Scout Cavalry, so do not take long deer pushes in this build.
If the opponent goes heavy on archers in Feudal, delay Castle Age a little and add Skirmishers before the Eagle switch.
Do not trade Men-at-Arms evenly with villagers; the goal is idle time for the enemy.
beaten_by: A Militia drush from the opponent arrives before your Men-at-Arms are ready. Wall the important parts, garrison if needed, and send your own Militia into their base instead of fighting theirs. Towers at the wood line and early Skirmishers blunt the Men-at-Arms, and a fast Scout opening punishes Archers without Spearmen. If you scout Scouts, add two or three Spearmen from the Barracks before the Archery Range.

title: Bengalis Arena Fast Castle Boom (25+2)
summary: A safe fast castle for Arena and other closed maps. The Bengali Town Center spawns two villagers on Feudal and two more on Castle, your starting stone pays for two extra Town Centers, and the Imperial Age then spawns six more villagers.
description:
Bengalis are one of the best booming civilizations on closed maps because every age up gives two free villagers per Town Center. This build is the classic 25+2 Arena fast castle with three Town Centers, adjusted for that bonus.

You click Feudal Age at 25 pop. The two villagers that spawn when the Feudal Age arrives go straight to gold, and you train two more during the Feudal Age, so you click Castle Age with 28 villagers. The Castle Age adds two more. The 200 stone you start with covers the stone cost of two extra Town Centers, so you never have to mine stone for this boom.

After the boom, you can push with Monks and Armored Elephants or Siege Elephants, take a Castle for Rathas, or keep booming and click Imperial Age, where three Town Centers spawn six villagers at once.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; send the Scout Cavalry to find the sheep
First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries, and stays there
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries in total)
Next 3 villagers on boar and sheep; lure the second boar when the first is nearly done
Move sheep villagers onto Farms around the Town Center as the sheep run out
Next 4 villagers build a second Lumber Camp (8 on wood in total)
Next 2 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Click up to the Feudal Age at 25 pop (24 villagers and the Scout Cavalry)
While the age loads, keep seeding Farms until you have about 4 to 6
Feudal Age arrives: the Town Center spawns 2 free villagers. Send both to gold (4 on gold)
Two wood villagers build a Market and a Blacksmith, then go back to wood
Train 2 more villagers and send them to wood
Click up to the Castle Age as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold (28 villagers)
While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar; move a few sheep or berry villagers to gold
Castle Age arrives: 2 more villagers spawn. Use them and a few wood villagers to build two Town Centers; your starting 200 stone covers both
Research Bow Saw, then Wheelbarrow once the new Town Centers are working; buy food at the Market if the Town Centers would go idle
Keep adding Farms to about 25, then grow gold to about 10 villagers and research Gold Mining

after_feudal: With three Town Centers working you have a choice. Against a passive opponent, keep booming to around 70 villagers and click Imperial Age; the six villagers that spawn when it arrives are a big lead. Against an opponent who pushes, add a Monastery and use Monks with their +3/+3 armor, then a Castle for Rathas and Paiks. Battle Elephants with Bloodlines and Husbandry are your strongest push unit, and Siege Elephants take down a walled Arena base.
tips: Do not spend your starting stone. It pays for both Castle Age Town Centers.
Know where the free villagers go before each age up: gold in Feudal, Town Center foundations in Castle.
Buy food at the Market in the early Castle Age so three Town Centers never stop producing.
The Imperial Age gives two villagers for every Town Center you own, so a fourth Town Center is a fair choice if you are safe.
Arena walls protect you from most early aggression, but scout for a Monk or siege push around the 20 minute mark.
beaten_by: A fast Monk and siege push or a Castle Age Knight push before your Town Centers are finished. Scout the opponent's age up time. If they reach Castle Age first, build one Town Center instead of two and spend the rest on Monks, Spearmen and a Castle. On open maps, this build is too greedy against Feudal aggression unless you wall.

title: Bengalis Scouts (19 pop, plus 2 free Villagers)
summary: A standard 19 pop Scout opening where the two Villagers that spawn on reaching the Feudal Age build your Stable right away. Your scouts do extra damage to Skirmishers, so the usual answer to a scout rush works poorly against you.
description:
This is the common Bengali opening on Arabia. The Dark Age is a normal 19 pop scout build, since the Bengali bonus does nothing until the age arrives. When the Feudal Age lands, your Town Center spawns two extra Villagers. Use them to build the Stable at once, so no wood villager has to stop working and the first Scout Cavalry comes out on time.

Bengali cavalry deals +2 damage to Skirmishers. Most players answer scouts with Spearmen and Skirmishers, and your scouts can keep killing those Skirmishers while you avoid the Spearmen. Raid wood and gold, take fights with Skirmishers, and run from groups of Spearmen.

The build sets up a Castle Age where you spawn two more Villagers. Use them to start a second Town Center, then pick Rathas, Battle Elephants or Monks depending on what you scouted.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; queue villagers and send the Scout Cavalry to find the sheep
First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 10 lures the first boar to the Town Center
Next 2 villagers on sheep or boar under the Town Center
Villager 13 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries, and stays there
Next 2 villagers on berries (3 on berries in total)
When the first boar is almost eaten, a villager from under the Town Center lures the second boar; villager 16 goes under the Town Center
Next 2 villagers to wood (5 on wood in total)
Click up to the Feudal Age at 19 pop (18 villagers and the Scout Cavalry); skip Loom
While the age loads, one wood villager builds a Barracks; as sheep run out, move those villagers to wood and start Farms
Feudal Age arrives: the Town Center spawns 2 free villagers. Send both to build a Stable near your wood, then to wood
Make Scout Cavalry nonstop from the Stable
Research Double-Bit Axe, then Horse Collar when you have the food
New villagers go to wood and Farms until you have about 8 Farms
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Add a Blacksmith and Forging if you keep fighting; otherwise bank food and gold for the Castle Age
Click up to the Castle Age at about 28 to 30 villagers, with 2 or 3 villagers on stone so you can afford a second Town Center

after_feudal:
Raid with the scouts in a group of four to six. Look for Skirmishers to kill and avoid Spearmen and Town Center fire. Keep your Town Center working the whole time.

When the Castle Age arrives the Town Center spawns two more villagers. Send them with a few wood villagers to build a second Town Center. Then choose your Castle Age unit. Rathas from a Castle work against most armies if you watch their mode. Battle Elephants with Bloodlines and Husbandry are strong against infantry and push buildings. Monks with their extra armor are a good answer to Knights. Light Cavalry keeps raiding and still gets +2 against Skirmishers.
tips: Decide before you click Feudal where the two free villagers will build the Stable; idle time on them wastes the bonus.
Your scouts deal +2 damage to Skirmishers, so you do not have to run from Skirmishers the way other scout civilizations do.
Groups of Spearmen still beat your scouts; go around them and hit another resource.
The Castle Age also spawns two villagers per Town Center, so a second Town Center pays back faster for you than for most civilizations.
Bengalis have no Hussar; plan on Light Cavalry for the rest of the game.
beaten_by: A fast archer opening with walls is the biggest problem, because scouts cannot catch archers behind palisades. Switch to Skirmishers of your own and click Castle Age early. Men-at-Arms into towers also hurt, since the Bengalis have no Dark Age bonus; keep a few villagers ready to build a palisade and add Spearmen. Against an opponent who walls completely, stop at four or five scouts and go up to the Castle Age.

title: Berbers Fast Castle Knights (27+2)
summary: The standard Berber plan: a clean fast Castle Age with two Stables ready, then Knights that cost 15% less than anyone else's.
description:
The Dark Age is the usual 27 villager fast Castle build. The Berber bonuses change what happens after it: Knights cost about 51 food and 64 gold in the Castle Age, so the same economy keeps two Stables busy with gold to spare for Bloodlines, Husbandry or a third Stable. The faster villagers do not change the villager split, but every walk is shorter, so the build is a little more forgiving when your sheep are spread out or your woodline is far.

Pick it on open maps against opponents who will not rush you hard, in the pocket of team games, and on closed maps where you can wall. Against an aggressive Feudal player, wall the woodline and gold with palisades and houses before clicking up, or switch to a Scouts into Knights opening.

You can cut the Dark Age to 25 or 26 villagers once the build is clean. Below that, the Castle Age economy gets too thin to pay for two Stables.

First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar to the Town Center
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill at the berries, and forages there
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 in total); lure the second boar when the first is about half eaten
Next 2 villagers on boar or sheep under the Town Center
When sheep run low, move the most damaged sheep villagers onto Farms around the Town Center
Next 6 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (10 on wood)
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp and mine gold
Research Loom while you finish collecting 500 food
Click up to the Feudal Age with 27 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, one wood villager builds a Barracks; keep seeding Farms as the sheep and boar run out until you have about 9 Farms
Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build a Stable and a Blacksmith right away
The next 2 villagers go to gold (5 on gold)
Click up to the Castle Age as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold
While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar
New villagers go to gold; when the berries run out, move 3 of those villagers to gold and the rest onto Farms
Build a second Stable before the Castle Age arrives and finish your walls
Castle Age lands around 15:00 for most players. Queue Knights from both Stables at once; at 51 food and 64 gold each, you can keep both busy with about 8 gold miners

after_feudal: Start Knights from both Stables the moment the Castle Age lands and keep the Town Center making villagers. Send the next four or five villagers to gold and get Gold Mining. Research Bloodlines once you have five or six Knights, then Husbandry, which suits Berber raids well. Hit wood lines and farms with all the Knights together and leave when Pikemen arrive. Because the Knights are cheaper, most Berber players add a third Town Center or a third Stable behind the first raid. If the opponent shows mass Pikemen, switch to Crossbowmen or start a Castle for Camel Archers; against Cavalry Archer civilizations, Camel Archers are the plan anyway.
tips: Wall before you click to the Castle Age; you have almost no army in the Feudal Age.
The faster villagers help the most with walling and with building the Stable and Blacksmith on time, so use them for that.
Keep the Knights in one group. A lone Knight does little against villagers who fight back.
The cavalry discount also covers Camel Riders and the Scout Cavalry line, so against an enemy Knight rush, cheap Camel Riders are a strong answer.
If you see a Feudal rush coming, drop a few Spearmen or Skirmishers and delay the Castle Age rather than losing villagers.
beaten_by: A Feudal rush that lands before your walls are up hurts the most, since scouts or archers kill villagers while you have no army. In the Castle Age, massed Pikemen, Camel Riders and Monks hold Knights well. Against heavy pikes, switch to Crossbowmen or Camel Archers and play for the economy with extra Town Centers.

title: Bohemians Fast Castle into Hand Cannoneers (27+2)
summary: A standard fast Castle Age that uses the 50 wood Blacksmith and free Gold Mining, then turns into Castle Age Hand Cannoneers with Pikemen in front and a Monastery for Fervor.
description:
The Bohemians are the only civilization that can research Chemistry and train Hand Cannoneers in the Castle Age, and this build gets you there quickly. The Dark Age is a normal 27 villager fast Castle. The differences come in the Feudal Age: your Blacksmith costs only 50 wood, and Gold Mining is free and active the moment the age arrives, so the 200 gold for Castle Age comes in faster.

Pick it on Arena, Black Forest, Hideout and other closed maps, and on Arabia when you can wall your wood and gold lines. On open maps against a scout or archer rush, keep a few Spearmen or Skirmishers ready and accept a later Castle time.

Once in Castle Age you build a 100 wood University, research Chemistry and start Hand Cannoneers from two Archery Ranges. Pikemen go in front, a Monastery gives you Fervor for faster villagers and Monks against Knights, and a third Town Center behind the first push is a common follow up.

Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood

Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries, and stays there

Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold and mine

While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar
New villagers go to gold; when the berries run out, move those villagers to Farms
Castle Age arrives at about 16 minutes; Gold Shaft Mining and Stone Shaft Mining are free from now on
Two wood villagers build a University (100 wood) and research Chemistry; start Hand Cannoneers and a few Pikemen

after_feudal: In Castle Age the order is University, Chemistry, then Hand Cannoneers from the Archery Range while a second range goes up. Keep about 10 to 12 villagers on gold, since Hand Cannoneers cost 50 gold each and Chemistry costs 200 more. Train Pikemen from the Barracks as a front line; your spears deal extra bonus damage, so a handful stops Knights from reaching your gunpowder. Build a Monastery and research Fervor and Sanctity, which speed up and toughen your villagers and give you Monks against cavalry. If your opponent masses Crossbowmen, add Mangonels and Skirmishers. With a Castle, research Wagenburg Tactics and consider a few Hussite Wagons to absorb arrows. Take a third Town Center once your army can hold the map.
tips: Place the Blacksmith and Archery Range the second Feudal Age lands; you only need 225 wood for both.
Do not plan food or wood for Gold Mining or Stone Mining; the Bohemians get every Mining Camp technology for free.
Hand Cannoneers miss part of their shots, so attack melee units with them and leave archers to Mangonels and Skirmishers.
Fervor is worth getting early even if you never make Monks, because it speeds up every villager.
On Arabia, wall the wood and gold lines before you click Castle Age; you have almost no army in the Feudal Age.
beaten_by: A Feudal rush that reaches you before your walls are closed is the biggest danger, especially archers, which kill villagers while you have nothing at home. In Castle Age, massed Crossbowmen with Skirmishers trade well against Hand Cannoneers, and Mangonels punish a clumped gunpowder army. Answer archers with your own Mangonels and Skirmishers, and spread the Hand Cannoneers out. Cavalry archer civilizations are the worst matchup; stay close to Castles and push with siege.

title: Britons One Range Archers
summary: A quick archer opening that uses the Briton shepherd bonus to click up early, starts archers from one Archery Range and adds a second range once gold income is up.
description:
This is the generic one range archer build with the Briton changes worked in. Your shepherds work 25% faster, so the sheep give food quicker than for other civilizations and you reach the Feudal Age sooner with the same villager split. Your Archery Ranges also work 10% faster, so you need slightly more villagers on gold than the generic build to keep production going.

Start archers as soon as the Feudal Age lands and send the first few forward to slow down the opponent's walls. Once 6 to 8 archers have Fletching, attack wood and gold lines.

The build is the default for Britons on Arabia and other open maps. On closed maps a Fast Castle is usually better. If you scout an early Men-at-Arms or Drush, the first archers from this build come out early enough to defend.

title: Bulgarians Fast Castle Krepost Rush
strategy: Fast Castle into Krepost and Konniks
summary: A Fast Castle that mines stone in Feudal, drops a Krepost near the opponent as soon as the Castle Age arrives and pours Konniks out of it, with a cheap second Town Center at home.
description:
The Krepost costs 350 stone, a little more than half a Castle, and it can be built the moment you reach the Castle Age. Placed near the opponent's gold or wood, it kills villagers by itself and trains Konniks in 16 seconds each. Bulgarian Town Centers also cost only 50 stone, so the same stone income pays for a second Town Center at home.

The Dark Age is a normal 27 villager Fast Castle. The difference is in Feudal: you send villagers to stone instead of the usual all-food setup, and you skip the Stable. Many players also build a Market to buy the last stone or food for the age up.

Use it against opponents who boom or play a slow Feudal game, and on closed maps where walls keep you safe. It is an all-in in the sense that you have no army until the Krepost stands, so wall your base before you click up.

First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on berries
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 in total); lure the second boar with a sheep villager
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar
Next 5 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (9 on wood); move worn out shepherds onto Farms
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Villager 27 goes to stone and builds a Mining Camp there
Research Loom and click up to the Feudal Age with 27 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, wall your wood and gold lines with Houses and palisades, and keep seeding Farms
Feudal Age arrives: build a Blacksmith and a Market with wood villagers
Move 2 more villagers to stone (3 on stone) and send the new ones to gold
Click up to the Castle Age with 800 food and 200 gold; use the Market if one resource is short
While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar
New villagers to gold and stone; you want 350 stone for the Krepost and 50 for a Town Center
Castle Age arrives: send 4 or 5 wood villagers forward to build a Krepost near the opponent's gold or wood
One villager builds a second Town Center at home
Train Konniks from the Krepost nonstop and research Bloodlines at a Stable once you can spare the food

after_feudal:
Keep the Krepost villagers next to it to repair while it is under attack, and send them home once the first five or six Konniks are out. Use the Konniks to clear anything that comes near the Krepost, then raid villagers on the nearest resource. Stirrups is researched at a Castle, so build one at home once your stone income allows it.

At home, keep both Town Centers making villagers and add a third Town Center when you have 50 more stone. Blacksmith upgrades cost half the food, so get Forging and Scale Barding Armor early. If the opponent masses Pikemen or Camel Riders, add Long Swordsmen, which you get for free, and Skirmishers from a Range.
tips: Pick a Krepost spot behind the opponent's resources, out of reach of their Town Center.
Build the Krepost with at least 4 villagers so it finishes before the opponent can react.
Konniks leave a Dismounted Konnik when they die, so fight close to the Krepost where the infantry form survives.
Do not forget your own villager production while you micro the push.
If the opponent scouts the stone mining and starts a Feudal rush, stay home and wall; a late Krepost is still strong.
beaten_by: A Feudal rush that arrives before your walls are up hurts this build badly, since you skip Feudal army. Archers and Skirmishers on your stone line are the most common punishment. Later, a fast Monk response or many Pikemen around the Krepost slow the Konniks. If the push stalls, turn the game into a boom with your cheap Town Centers and switch to Long Swordsmen and Siege Rams.

title: Bulgarians Men-at-Arms into Scouts (20 pop)
summary: Click up at 20 population, get Men-at-Arms for free the moment Feudal Age arrives and follow with a Stable for Scout Cavalry. The free upgrade puts your infantry in the enemy base much earlier than a normal Men-at-Arms rush.

The Dark Age split is food heavy: six on sheep, four on berries, two boars and only three on wood. Most of the wood comes later, when you move shepherds to the trees during the age up. The Barracks goes up late in the Dark Age and you queue the Militia while the Feudal Age researches.

Pick this build on open maps when you expect your opponent to go for a Fast Castle or a slow archer start. After the Men-at-Arms, a single Stable lets you add Scout Cavalry and pick off villagers the infantry cannot catch.

Forging and Scale Barding Armor cost half the food at your Blacksmith, so research them early. Once your opponent has walls up and Spearmen out, pull the Men-at-Arms home to guard your own wood and keep raiding with the scouts.

Aim to click Castle Age around 30 villagers with 2 or 3 villagers on stone. In the Castle Age your Men-at-Arms become Long Swordsmen for free, Town Centers cost only 50 stone, and Knights with Stirrups or a Krepost with Konniks continue the pressure.

If the opponent has archers and palisades before your Men-at-Arms arrive, stop attacking walls, add Skirmishers from a Range, and go up to the Castle Age where Knights and Long Swordsmen take over. Towers at the opponent's gold also stop the infantry; answer them by going up, since Bulgarians have no early siege.

title: Burgundians Fast Castle into Cavaliers (27+2)
summary: A Fast Castle that buys Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar in the Dark Age, reaches the Castle Age with two Stables and turns the first Knights into Cavaliers a few minutes later.
description:

Pick it on closed maps, in the pocket position of team games, or on open maps when you expect a slow opponent and can wall. Against a fast Feudal rush, put up palisades around the wood and gold lines before you click up, and keep a few Flemish Militia from the Barracks in mind as an emergency answer to Scout Cavalry.

title: Burgundians Scouts into Cavaliers (21 pop)
summary: A Scout Cavalry opening with Double-Bit Axe in the Dark Age. The scouts hold map control and slow the opponent while your early upgrades carry you to a Cavalier timing in the Castle Age.
description:
The Burgundians need time to let their cheap upgrades pay off, and a Scout Cavalry opening buys that time on open maps. You go up a little later than a normal scout rush because Double-Bit Axe costs a bit of food in the Dark Age, but your wood economy is stronger in the Feudal Age, and you can add Horse Collar and Bow Saw early without hurting production. Stable technologies are half price, so Light Cavalry later and the Castle Age Cavalier upgrade both come cheap.

The idea is to deny the opponent's woodlines and berries with four to six Scout Cavalry, wall your own base behind them, and click up to the Castle Age around 19 to 20 minutes. From there the Stable is already built, and the scouts are replaced by Knights and then Cavaliers.

Morley Games and Hera both published Burgundian scouts into Cavalier builds after the 2021 bonus changes. The discount has since been reduced to 40 percent, so this version goes up one or two villagers later than those videos.

Once all sheep are found, push two or three deer to the Town Center with the scout if you can

Build a Blacksmith and research Forging if the scouts are still trading well
Click up to the Castle Age with about 30 villagers; research Heavy Plow while the age loads
Build a second Stable before the Castle Age arrives
In the Castle Age, start Knights from both Stables and research the Cavalier upgrade as soon as you can

after_feudal: Keep making Scout Cavalry from one Stable until the opponent has Spearmen or walls up; after that, stop, and spend food on Farms and the Castle click. Move the scouts to your own base to watch for counterattacks and kill any villagers walking to forward gold. In the Castle Age, make Knights from two Stables, research Cavalier and Husbandry, and use the old Scout Cavalry as a second raiding group or turn them into Light Cavalry later. Add a third Town Center when the first Cavaliers are out and your opponent is busy defending.

When that happens, pull back, add Skirmishers and go up to the Castle Age with your economy lead. A drush that hits your wood line before the scouts are out costs you villagers, so keep Loom available and pull villagers into the Town Center if needed.

title: Celts Fast Castle Siege Push (27+2)
summary: A 27+2 fast castle into two Siege Workshops. Celt siege fires 25% faster and the Siege Workshops work faster, so a Celt ram and Mangonel push with infantry hits harder and sooner than the same push from most civilizations.
description:
This build goes straight to the Castle Age and turns the Celt siege bonuses into an early push. You reach the Castle Age around the 15 to 16 minute mark with two Siege Workshops ready to start. Rams take down the opponent's Town Center, towers and Castles, while Mangonels deal with the archers that usually stop infantry.

Celt siege fires 25% faster, the team bonus makes your Siege Workshops work 20% faster, and your infantry moves 15% faster in the Castle Age, so the army stays together on the way. The lumberjack bonus helps the whole plan, because rams, Mangonels and Siege Workshops are wood heavy.

The push is strongest on closed maps like Arena and Black Forest, and against opponents who wall on open maps. Think of it as a Celt version of the classic siege and infantry fast castle; on open maps, wall before you click the Castle Age.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; send the Scout Cavalry to find the sheep
First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries, and stays there
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 on berries in total)
Next 2 villagers on boar and sheep; lure the second boar with a boar villager
As sheep run low, move the most damaged sheep villagers onto Farms around the Town Center
Next 6 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (10 on wood in total)
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Research Loom while you collect the last of the 500 food
Click up to the Feudal Age at 28 pop (27 villagers and the Scout Cavalry)
During the age up, one wood villager builds a Barracks; keep seeding Farms with sheep villagers until about 9 Farms
Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build a Blacksmith and a Market
Next 2 villagers to gold (5 on gold)
Click up to the Castle Age as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold
While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar; bank about 400 wood for two Siege Workshops
New villagers to gold; when berries run out, move 3 of those villagers to gold and the rest onto Farms
Castle Age arrives: two wood villagers build two Siege Workshops near the front of your base
Make 2 Battering Rams first, then Mangonels; train Pikemen or Long Swordsmen from the Barracks to guard the siege
Research Bow Saw and Gold Mining, then infantry armor at the Blacksmith

after_feudal:
Move out as soon as you have two rams, two Mangonels and six to eight infantry. Walk to a Town Center or a forward building and let the rams work while the Mangonels shoot any archers that come in. Keep the infantry between the siege and the opponent's army. If cavalry comes for the siege, the Pikemen take the fight.

Upgrade to Capped Ram when you have the gold, and add Long Swordsman if the opponent makes infantry. Once the push has done damage, build a Castle for Woad Raiders and Stronghold, add Town Centers at home, and get Furor Celtica before the Imperial Age so your siege lasts longer.
tips: Build the Siege Workshops toward the opponent so the siege does not have to walk across the whole map.
Rams first, then Mangonels: rams win the game against a single Town Center, Mangonels protect them from archers.
Do not leave the Mangonels in front of your own infantry; Celt Mangonels fire fast and friendly fire hurts.
If the opponent has many Knights, make more Pikemen and fewer Mangonels.
Wall your base before clicking the Castle Age on open maps; you have almost no army until the push is ready.
beaten_by: Feudal aggression before your walls are up, because you have no army until the Castle Age. A fast Knight push that reaches your Siege Workshops before you have Pikemen is also hard. In the Castle Age, Light Cavalry or Knights flanking the siege, Monks converting rams, and a Castle near the opponent's Town Center all slow the push. If the push is stopped, keep the siege at home for defense and boom with two more Town Centers.

title: Celts Men-at-Arms into Archers
summary: Three Militia in the Dark Age, Men-at-Arms the moment you reach Feudal, then two Archery Ranges paid for by the Celt wood bonus. Celt infantry moves 10% faster in Feudal, so the Men-at-Arms arrive sooner and catch more villagers.
description:
This is the standard Men-at-Arms into Archers opening with the Celt bonuses taken into account. You train three Militia at the end of the Dark Age, upgrade them to Men-at-Arms right after the Feudal Age arrives, and hit the opponent's wood or gold. Meanwhile you build two Archery Ranges and follow up with archers.

Celt infantry moves 5% faster in the Dark Age and 10% faster in the Feudal Age. That makes the Men-at-Arms better at running down villagers and at escaping from archers. Celt lumberjacks work 15% faster, so the wood for the second Lumber Camp, two Archery Ranges and Farms comes in sooner than in the generic build.

Pick it on Arabia and other open maps against civilizations with a slow start, or when you expect a fast castle. The Men-at-Arms tell you what the opponent is doing, which decides whether you follow with archers or Skirmishers. From the Castle Age, Celt archers fall behind, so plan to change into infantry and siege.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; send the Scout Cavalry to find the sheep and look for the opponent's sheep too
First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries in total)
Villager 16 lures the second boar when the first is nearly done
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar
Villager 19 builds a Barracks, then goes to wood; queue 3 Militia as soon as the Barracks is done
Villager 20 builds a Mining Camp on gold and mines
Villager 21 goes to gold (2 on gold)
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age at 25 pop (21 villagers, the Scout Cavalry and 3 Militia)
While the age loads, walk the 3 Militia to the opponent's base; move 4 sheep villagers to a second Lumber Camp
Feudal Age arrives: research Men-at-Arms at the Barracks and Double-Bit Axe at the Lumber Camp
Attack wood or gold with the Men-at-Arms; make 1 or 2 more if the opponent fights back with villagers
Move the last sheep villagers onto Farms; new villagers go to gold (about 5 on gold)
Two wood villagers build two Archery Ranges, then a Blacksmith
Make archers nonstop from both Archery Ranges; research Fletching once you have 4 or 5
Keep adding villagers to Farms and gold; Horse Collar when food allows

after_feudal:
Use the Men-at-Arms to force villagers off wood or gold, then pull them back to defend when the opponent's response arrives. Join the archers with them once you have six or so archers.

If the opponent answers with archers of their own, switch the ranges to Skirmishers. If they go Scout Cavalry, add a few Spearmen and keep the archers behind them.

Click the Castle Age at about 30 to 32 villagers. In the Castle Age, upgrade to Long Swordsman or Pikeman depending on the opponent, add a Siege Workshop and make Mangonels or Scorpions. Your archers can keep fighting in the early Castle Age with Crossbowman and Bodkin Arrow, but stop adding them once the game goes long.
tips: Celt Men-at-Arms are faster than villagers, so chase villagers that run instead of hitting buildings.
The extra wood lets you add a tower on your gold or at the opponent's wood if your Men-at-Arms are stuck at a wall.
Look for the opponent's sheep with your scout in the Dark Age; Celts can steal them even with the opponent's scout next to them.
Do not overbuild archers. Celt archers lack Thumb Ring and Bracer, so they are a Feudal and early Castle Age tool.
Men-at-Arms lose badly to archers; retreat them when you see five or more.
beaten_by: A fast archer opening with walls holds Men-at-Arms easily and then outranges your own archers later. Against it, switch to Skirmishers and go up to the Castle Age sooner. A Scout Cavalry player can ignore your Men-at-Arms and raid your archers' economy, so keep a few Spearmen at home. Drush into fast castle is also annoying because the opponent walls before your Men-at-Arms arrive; in that case use them to defend and boom.

title: Chinese Archers (24 pop)
summary: A Chinese start into two Archery Ranges at 24 population, the opening that leads most naturally into Crossbowmen and the Chinese archer late game.
description:
This build uses the same Chinese start as the scout opening: Loom first, every villager on sheep, and no House until about 13 population because the Town Center supports 15. The difference comes at the end of the Dark Age. You make one more villager, put most of the extra ones on wood, and click up with a heavy wood economy and three villagers going to gold, which is what two Archery Ranges need.

Archers fit the Chinese well. Fletching, the Blacksmith armor and every later archer upgrade cost less, and the Archers turn into Crossbowmen in the Castle Age without any change of production. The build also suits the flank position in team games.

If the opponent opens with Scout Cavalry, add a Spearman or two from the Barracks and keep the Archers near your woodline until you have six or more.

steps.text: Research Loom at once; the Town Center cannot train villagers until you have food
All 6 starting villagers go to sheep under the Town Center; no House yet
Villager 7 also goes to sheep; force a food drop off only when the Town Center is about to go idle
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 goes to wood (4 on wood)
Villager 13 builds a House, then a Mill at the berries, and forages there
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 on berries in total)
Villager 18 goes to boar; lure the second boar when the first is about half eaten
A wood villager builds a second House before you reach 20 population
Next 5 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (9 on wood)
Click up to the Feudal Age with 23 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, move sheep and boar villagers so you have about 12 on wood and 3 on gold with a Mining Camp
One wood villager builds a Barracks during the age up
Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build the first Archery Range, then a second one right after
Start Archers from both ranges and keep them in one group
Research Double-Bit Axe, then Fletching once you have a few Archers out; both cost 5% less for the Chinese
New villagers go to Farms as the food under the Town Center runs out, with a couple more to gold

after_feudal: Most players have six Archers and Fletching out between 13:30 and 14:30. Push to the opponent's woodline or gold with the group, use the Archers to protect your own woodline from Scouts, and add Horse Collar and Farms behind them. Aim to click the Castle Age with around 20 Archers, then research Crossbowman and Bodkin Arrow right away; both cost 10% less in the Castle Age. From there, build Town Centers and choose between more Crossbowmen, Knights against Skirmishers, or a Castle for Chu Ko Nu.
tips: Keep the Archers together and away from enemy Scouts until Fletching is done.
If the opponent makes many Skirmishers, stop adding Archers and switch to Scout Cavalry or Men-at-Arms, or go up to the Castle Age and make Knights.
Villager 7 on sheep matters. Six shepherds cannot keep up with constant villager production.
The build needs a lot of wood early; do not take villagers off wood in the Feudal Age until both ranges are up and Houses are covered.
beaten_by: A fast Men-at-Arms or drush can catch the Chinese start with too few resources. Skirmishers in numbers stop Archers cold; answer with Scout Cavalry, Men-at-Arms or a quick Castle Age. Strong archer civilizations like the Britons or Ethiopians win an even Feudal archer fight, so keep your Archers near towers or your Town Center until the Castle Age discount takes over.

title: Chinese Scouts (23 pop)
summary: The standard Chinese opening: Loom first, all villagers on sheep, then a Feudal Age at 23 population with a Stable ready for Scout Cavalry.
description:
The Chinese start with 6 villagers and the Scout Cavalry, but with 0 food and 150 wood. The Town Center cannot make a villager until food comes in, so you research Loom right away and get every villager onto sheep as fast as the scout can find them. The Town Center supports 15 population, which means no Houses in the first minutes and more wood left for the Lumber Camp and Mill.

After that the build looks like a normal scout opening. You reach the Feudal Age with 22 villagers, put most of the food villagers onto wood during the age up and make Scout Cavalry from one Stable. The tech discount makes Bloodlines and the Feudal economy upgrades slightly cheaper, and the Scouts give you map control while your economy catches up with the extra villagers.

Practise the first three minutes against the AI. The opening punishes idle time more than any other civilization's, and a far-away sheep or a lamed boar can put you behind.

steps.text: Research Loom at once; with 0 food the Town Center has nothing else to do
All 6 starting villagers go to the sheep the scout brings in; no House is needed yet because the Town Center supports 15 population
When Loom finishes and you reach 50 food, queue villagers. Force a drop off at the Town Center only when it is about to go idle
Villager 7 also goes to sheep so the food keeps up with villager production
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 11 lures the first boar; you may need to lure it a little earlier than usual
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill at the berries, and forages there
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 on berries in total)
Next 2 villagers on boar; lure the second boar when the first is about half eaten
A wood villager builds a second House before you reach 20 population; move one damaged sheep villager to a Farm when the sheep run out
Next 4 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (7 on wood)
Click up to the Feudal Age with 22 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, move 4 boar and sheep villagers to wood (about 11 on wood) and add a second Farm
One wood villager builds a Barracks during the age up
Feudal Age arrives: build a Stable with two wood villagers and start Scout Cavalry nonstop
Research Double-Bit Axe, then Horse Collar; the Chinese pay 5% less for every Feudal technology
New villagers go to Farms as the berries and hunt run out, then a few to gold
Research Bloodlines once you have five or six Scout Cavalry

after_feudal: Use the Scout Cavalry to kill or chase villagers on wood and gold, take the map and protect your own woodlines. Keep the Town Center busy and move toward 15 to 18 Farms. Most players click the Castle Age between 17:30 and 19:00 with 8 or so Scouts and Bloodlines done. In the Castle Age, the cheaper upgrades suit a Knight follow-up if you saw few Pikemen, or a switch to Crossbowmen if the opponent went heavy on Spearmen and walls. Add Town Centers as soon as you can; each one gives 15 population, so you need fewer Houses during the boom.
tips: Practise the first two minutes against the AI until the Town Center never goes idle after Loom.
Send the scout straight for the sheep. The Chinese start depends on the first sheep arriving quickly.
Do not build the first House too early. With 15 population from the Town Center, the first House is due around 13 population.
If the boar is far or the opponent steals it, put the next villagers on berries and sheep instead and click up one or two villagers later.
The Chinese have no Hussar line past Light Cavalry, so the Scouts are for the Feudal Age; plan Knights or Crossbowmen for later.
beaten_by: A fast drush or Men-at-Arms rush that hits during the awkward Chinese start is the biggest threat, since you have fewer resources early. Spearmen behind walls or towers on your Scouts slow the build down; switch the Stable time into Archers or Skirmishers and go up to the Castle Age instead.

title: Cumans Feudal Second Town Center Boom (19 pop)
summary: Click up early, drop a second Town Center as soon as the Feudal Age lands and run two Town Centers into a Castle Age at about 20 minutes with 50 to 60 villagers.
description:
Only the Cumans can build a second Town Center in the Feudal Age. This build goes up quickly with 18 villagers, saves wood during the age up and puts the new Town Center down the moment Feudal Age arrives. From then on both Town Centers make villagers nonstop, and you click Castle Age at about 19 to 20 minutes with a much bigger economy than a normal fast Castle player.

It is strongest on closed maps and against opponents who fast Castle or boom. On Arabia you must scout first: if you see an early Barracks, Archery Range or a forward tower, skip the second Town Center or delay it and make units. Wall your wood and food with palisades, which have extra hit points for Cuman teams.

In Castle Age you have three common follow ups: keep booming to four or more Town Centers, make Knights or Steppe Lancers from three Stables, or go three or four Archery Ranges of Crossbowmen. Sources disagree on the Dark Age villager count, from 18 to 20; the 18 villager version below is the most common one today.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; scout for sheep, both boars and a good woodline near gold for the second Town Center
First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 10 lures the first boar
Villager 11 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries)
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar; lure the second boar and push any deer to the Town Center
Next 2 villagers go to wood (5 on wood)
Click up to the Feudal Age with 18 villagers plus the scout, without Loom unless you see a rush
During the age up, move 4 hunters to wood (9 on wood) so you have 275 wood when the age lands; you already have the 100 stone
Feudal Age arrives: 4 or 5 villagers build the second Town Center on a woodline or next to gold
Research Double-Bit Axe, then Horse Collar when the berries and hunt start to run out
New villagers from the first Town Center go to wood and start Farms; wall your wood and food lines with palisades
Second Town Center finishes: both Town Centers make villagers without stopping from now on
Send villagers to Farms until you have about 12 to 14 Farms, the rest to wood
Research Wheelbarrow in one Town Center while the other keeps making villagers
Put 6 to 8 villagers on gold; build a Blacksmith and a Stable (100 wood for Cumans) or a Market
Click up to the Castle Age from one Town Center at about 19 to 20 minutes; the other keeps making villagers
Decide the follow up during the age up: more Town Centers, two more Stables for Knights or Steppe Lancers, or more Archery Ranges

after_feudal: In Castle Age, the boom follow up is two more Town Centers right away and a few Pikemen or Crossbowmen for safety; few civilizations can match a Cuman villager count this way. The aggressive follow up is three Stables with Bloodlines, which Cumans can afford quickly, then Knights or Steppe Lancers raiding in one big group. Research Steppe Husbandry at a Castle if you plan to mass Light Cavalry, Steppe Lancers or Cavalry Archers. Keep adding gold miners as the army grows and use a Capped Ram or two to crack Town Centers and Castles.
tips: Pick the second Town Center spot during the Dark Age so the builders walk straight there.
More builders finish the Town Center much faster; one villager alone needs 4 minutes 30 seconds.
Skip Loom in the Dark Age only if your scout has seen that your opponent is not rushing.
Click Castle Age from one Town Center so villager production never stops.
If you get rushed, the second Town Center still helps: place it near your first one so both can shoot at raiders.
beaten_by: A committed Feudal rush, especially Men-at-Arms, archers or a tower rush, arrives while your wood is tied up in the second Town Center and you have no army. Scouts that hit your woodline before the walls are closed also do a lot of damage. If you see aggression, delay the Town Center, make Spearmen, Skirmishers or archers, and drop it once the attack is held. A fast Castle Knight push with Mangonels at about 16 minutes also catches you before your Castle Age units are out.

title: Cumans Scouts into Feudal Rams (19 pop)
summary: Open Scout Cavalry from a 100 wood Stable, then add a Siege Workshop and two or three Battering Rams in the Feudal Age to break walls and threaten the Town Center of a player who is walling up for a fast Castle Age.
description:
The Cumans are the only civilization with Battering Rams in the Feudal Age. Rams take almost no damage from arrows, so a walled opponent with a few archers or Spearmen at home cannot stop them with ranged fire. Their real counters are melee units and villagers with Loom, and that is what your Scout Cavalry is for: when villagers run out to hit the rams, the scouts kill them.

The opening is a normal 19 pop scout build. The Cuman Stable costs 100 wood, so the first scouts come out a little earlier. While the scouts raid, you build a Blacksmith and a Siege Workshop and send two or three rams at the Town Center, the gold mining camp or the walls in front of the enemy economy.

Use it against opponents who wall and fast Castle, on Arabia or on closed maps like Arena where nobody expects a Feudal siege push. It needs a lot of wood and some gold, so a few villagers move from food to wood earlier than in a pure scout build. If the rams kill a Town Center or the walls, follow up with a second Town Center or a fast Castle Age while the opponent rebuilds.

steps.text: The three starting villagers build two Houses; scout for sheep and look at the enemy base early
First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 2 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop
Villager 9 builds a House, then lures the first boar
Villager 10 builds a Mill on the berries and gathers there
Next 6 villagers on sheep and boar; lure the second boar when the first runs low
Next 2 villagers go to wood (4 on wood)
Research Loom if you are short of 500 food, then click up to the Feudal Age with 18 villagers plus the scout
During the age up, move 5 hunters to wood (9 on wood) and 3 to berries
Halfway through the age up, one food villager builds a Barracks
Feudal Age arrives: two villagers build a Stable (100 wood for Cumans) towards the enemy and you start Scout Cavalry
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold and mine
Raid with the first 3 or 4 scouts, mainly to see the enemy walls and where the villagers work
With 150 wood, a wood villager builds a Blacksmith, then a Siege Workshop with the next 200 wood
Next 2 villagers go to gold (5 on gold); move sheep villagers onto Farms as the food runs out
Train two Battering Rams (160 wood and 75 gold each) and keep making a scout now and then
Send the rams with the scouts at about 14 to 15 minutes; hit the walls in front of the woodline or go straight at the Town Center
Keep the Town Center making villagers and add Farms; Horse Collar and Double-Bit Axe when the rams are paid for

after_feudal: Once the rams are in, the push decides the next step. If you kill the Town Center or a big part of the woodline, add a second Town Center at home and keep the pressure with scouts and a third ram. If the opponent holds with Spearmen and villagers, pull the rams back to break a wall somewhere else and click Castle Age; the Capped Ram upgrade and Knights or Steppe Lancers are the natural follow up. Keep at least 5 villagers on gold during the whole push.
tips: Rams can hold infantry; put a couple of Spearmen or Men-at-Arms inside if the enemy has scouts at home.
Target the walls in front of the woodline first if the Town Center is surrounded by villagers with Loom.
Never leave the rams alone. Keep the scouts next to them and kill every villager who comes out to fight.
If your opponent has towers, rams are the best answer you have in the Feudal Age.
Build the Siege Workshop close to the front so the rams do not walk across the whole map.
beaten_by: Massed melee units are the counter: Men-at-Arms, Spearmen and a big group of villagers with Loom kill Battering Rams fast, and your scouts lose to Spearmen. Against a player who opens with Men-at-Arms or Spearmen, keep the rams back until you have a few Men-at-Arms of your own, or skip the rams and go Scouts into a second Town Center. An archer rush that never lets you leave home also makes the ram investment too slow.

title: Danes Men-at-Arms into Skirmishers
summary: Click up at 19 pop with the Danish food bonus, hit with three cheap Men-at-Arms and Arson, burn buildings for loot when the villagers hide, then follow with Skirmishers or archers.
description:
This is the modern Men-at-Arms opening with the Danish bonuses worked in. The 5% food bonus makes the Dark Age smooth enough that 19 pop is an easy click, and the Man-at-Arms upgrade costs only about 14 gold, so you need less gold early than with other civilizations. Arson is also cheap in gold and makes your Men-at-Arms much better at their side job: burning down Lumber Camps, Mining Camps, Houses and Stables, which pays you 25% of each building's cost.

Use the Men-at-Arms to hit villagers first. When the villagers run to the Town Center, switch to the nearest camp or a building under construction. An opponent rarely deletes their own buildings to deny you the loot.

The follow up in this version is Skirmishers, which cost food and wood and suit the food bonus. Make archers instead if the opponent opens with Scout Cavalry or Knights.

steps.text: Starting villagers build two Houses; scout for sheep and deer
First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop; use the House as part of a wall
Villager 10 lures the first boar
Next 5 villagers on sheep and boar; lure the second boar and push 2 deer with the scout
Villager 16 builds a Barracks, then a House at the front of your base
Next 2 villagers on food under the Town Center
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age with 18 villagers plus the scout
While the age loads, 5 food villagers move to wood (8 on wood)
2 food villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Train 3 Militia from the Barracks so they are ready when the age lands
Feudal Age: research Man-at-Arms (only about 14 gold for Danes) and send the three out
Research Double-Bit Axe
Villager 20 builds a Mill at the berries
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 on berries)
Research Arson when you have the food; it costs very little gold for Danes
Once Arson and the upgrade are paid, move the 2 gold villagers to wood if you plan Skirmishers
Build an Archery Range and start Skirmishers (or archers against a cavalry opening)
New villagers to wood and farms; start farms as the hunt runs out
Build a Blacksmith and research Fletching, then Padded Archer Armor if you face archers

after_feudal:
Keep the Men-at-Arms alive and active: use them on villagers when possible and on buildings when not. Your Skirmishers protect them from archers. Add a Spearman or two if Scout Cavalry show up to chase the Skirmishers.

Wall while you pressure, add farms up to about a dozen, put villagers back on gold and click up to the Castle Age. In the Castle Age, build a Siege Workshop for a Battering Ram or Mangonels to keep killing buildings, then pick Mounted Crossbowmen against Knights or Knights against massed Skirmishers. Add Town Centers once your army has the opponent on the defensive.
tips: Three Men-at-Arms are usually enough; make a fourth only in a Men-at-Arms mirror or against strong infantry civilizations.
A Farm destroyed is a 75 wood swing: the opponent loses 60 and you gain 15.
Foundations and walls also pay out loot, so hit buildings that are going up.
Use the scout to block the opponent's villagers when the Men-at-Arms arrive.
A tower on your gold or wood line stops counter pressure while you push.
beaten_by: A quick wall with archers behind it, or an early tower on the opponent's resources, blunts the Men-at-Arms. Massed archers with Fletching also beat them in the open, which is why the Skirmishers follow so quickly. Against a fast Scout Cavalry opening, skip Skirmishers and make archers plus Spearmen. Against a Fast Castle, keep raiding buildings and go up yourself with a Siege Workshop ready.

title: Dravidians Men-at-Arms into Archers (20 pop)
summary: Three Militia before Feudal, a half price Man-at-Arms upgrade as soon as the age lands, and an Archery Range paid for by the 200 wood you receive on reaching Feudal.
description:
Two Dravidian bonuses make this opening cheaper than the generic version. Barracks technologies cost half, so the Man-at-Arms upgrade costs 50 food and 20 gold. On reaching the Feudal Age you also receive 200 wood, enough for an Archery Range the moment the age arrives, so you need fewer villagers on wood during the Dark Age.

The Men-at-Arms go out first to slow down the opponent's walls and military buildings. The archers follow a minute or two later and take over the pressure. Because you start with 100 gold, the three Militia and the upgrade need almost no mining; the gold villagers you add before the age up are for the archers. Population numbers in the steps count villagers plus the Scout Cavalry; the Militia come on top.

It is a good default on Arabia. If you scout an opponent going for Scouts, the same build works with Spearmen and Skirmishers from the Range instead of archers.

steps.text: The starting villagers build two Houses, then join the sheep; send the Scout Cavalry to find sheep
First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop
Villager 10 lures the first boar

tips: Spend the Feudal wood bonus straight away; it is meant for the Archery Range.

title: Ethiopians Archers (20 pop, two ranges)
summary: A two range archer rush that clicks up with 19 villagers and almost no gold miners, because the free 100 gold on reaching the Feudal Age pays for the first Archers.

The Ethiopians receive 100 food and 100 gold the moment they reach a new age. In a normal archer build you need three or four gold miners before you click up, just to have gold for the first Archers. Here the free gold does that job, so you can put those villagers on wood and food, click up two or three villagers earlier and still have Archers coming out of two ranges as soon as the age lands. Faster firing does the rest.

Use it on open maps when you want to take the initiative. Archers in the opponent's woodline at around 10 minutes force them to wall, make Skirmishers or pull villagers, and every one of those choices costs economy. Morley Games has published a 20 pop version, Jo Na a 19 pop version with an 8:50 uptime, and Age of Notes an 18 villager version for team games. summary: The standard knight rush with Frankish bonuses folded in: fewer villagers on berries, a free Horse Collar, and two Stables of Knights with 20% extra hit points around the 14 minute mark.

A second Stable goes up during the age up so both start Knights the moment you arrive. Morley Games plays a sharper version that lands near 12:45; the build below is a little slower and leaves room for Loom and a wall.

Wall your wood and gold with Palisades before you click Castle Age on open maps, because you have almost no army until the first Knights are out.

summary: A fast scout rush that puts seven villagers on berries to use the Frankish foraging bonus, reaches Feudal at 19 population and hits with Scout Cavalry that have 20% more hit points.

Seven villagers on berries give a steady food income while the sheep run out, and you click up at 19 population, two or three villagers earlier than a standard scout rush.

During the age up, most of the sheep villagers walk to the existing Lumber Camp so you have the wood for a Barracks and a Stable. The first Scouts arrive at the opponent's base around the time they are finishing their walls, which is the point of the build.

Pick it on open maps like Arabia against opponents who play slow, archer or fast castle openings. It is weaker against a civilization with a good early Spearman bonus or an aggressive drush.

summary: A very fast Feudal Age with every villager on food. The starting Mule Cart counts as a Dark Age building, so a Mill is all you build before clicking up at 16 villagers.

Both send most villagers to wood during the age up to pay for the Stable.

The Mule Cart also works as a second scout in the first minutes. It can take a few Town Center arrows, so you can send it toward the enemy base while your Scout Cavalry spends its time pushing deer. More deer means more Scouts later.

Pick it on open maps when you want early map control. Georgian mounted units also regenerate a little health in the Feudal Age, which helps Scouts that raid and retreat.

title: Goths Men-at-Arms (25 pop)
summary: Cheap Militia in the Dark Age, instant Loom, Men-at-Arms the moment you reach Feudal, then a second Barracks to keep the pressure going. A simple aggressive start that suits the Goths' cheap infantry and Barracks speed.
description:
Goth infantry is 15% cheaper in the Dark Age and 20% cheaper in the Feudal Age, and the Goth team bonus makes your own Barracks work 20% faster. That makes a Men-at-Arms opening cheaper for you than for anyone else, and you can keep adding units after the first hit. Loom is instant, so it costs you no Town Center time.

You make three Militia at the end of the Dark Age, click Feudal, upgrade to Men-at-Arms and attack the opponent's wood or gold. Goth infantry also has +1 attack against standard buildings in the Feudal Age, so if the opponent hides behind houses and palisades, your Men-at-Arms break through faster.

The follow-up is an Archery Range for Skirmishers, since Goth infantry has no Gambesons and dies to archers. Keep a few Men-at-Arms and Spearmen in the field, add Farms at home, and go to the Castle Age around 30 villagers.

after_feudal:
Your Men-at-Arms should kill villagers or force them into the Town Center, then pull back before archers catch them. When you see archers, stop making Men-at-Arms and switch the Archery Range to Skirmishers.

In the Castle Age, upgrade to Long Swordsman and Pikeman, add a Castle when the opponent goes heavy on archers, and train Huskarls. Build two more Town Centers if you are safe and add Barracks steadily so you have four by the time you click Imperial. Remember Goth defenses are weak, so keep units at home instead of relying on towers.

beaten_by: Archers behind palisades are the main answer to this build. Switch to Skirmishers and go up to the Castle Age instead of feeding more Men-at-Arms. A drush or a tower on your gold can also cancel the hit, so scout early. Against a fast castle you can do damage, but leave enough villagers at home to reach the Castle Age yourself, since Goth infantry is weak against Castle Age Knights without Plate Mail.

title: Gurjaras Scouts with the Forage Start (20 pop)
summary: Eat the two forage bushes under the Town Center first, put the sheep into a Mill at the main berries for a food trickle, and reach the Feudal Age at 20 population for Scout Cavalry.

The Gurjaras start with two forage bushes of 175 food under the Town Center and a Camel Scout. That changes the first minutes of a normal scout opening. Your first villagers forage under the Town Center instead of eating sheep, the Camel Scout pushes the sheep toward the main berries, and a Mill there takes the sheep in so they produce food over time. The boars carry the middle of the Dark Age.

The Feudal Age plan is ordinary Scout Cavalry from one Stable. The Gurjara bonus damage in the Feudal Age is small, so the scouts win through numbers and the food trickle keeps your farms later. You can also make a few Camel Scouts if the opponent answers with their own Scout Cavalry, and every Camel Scout becomes a free Camel Rider in the Castle Age.

Go up to the Castle Age with gold for Kshatriyas, and pick the Castle Age unit by what you see: Camel Riders against Knights, Shrivamsha Riders against archers, Chakram Throwers against Pikemen and infantry. Your Camel Scouts turn into Camel Riders for free when the age arrives, so they are never wasted.

summary: A 19 pop Scout Cavalry opening that uses cheaper Hindustani villagers to keep the Town Center busy, then a Castle Age with Camel Riders, Light Cavalry and extra Town Centers.
description:
This is the standard 19 pop scout build with the Hindustani discount on top. Villagers cost about 4 food less in the Dark Age and about 6 to 7 less in the Feudal Age, so you reach 500 food for the Feudal Age a little earlier and can keep the Town Center working while you pay for the Stable and the scouts. The Hindustani team bonus gives your scouts +2 attack against buildings, which lets them kill Houses and camps faster than other civilizations' scouts.

Use it on Arabia and other open maps when you want map control and to slow down the opponent's Feudal Age. The scouts are there to kill villagers, hunt down the enemy scout and keep your side of the map safe; they lose to Spearmen and walls, so leave as soon as the opponent has those.

The Hindustanis have no Knights, so the Castle Age follow up is Camel Riders against cavalry, Light Cavalry and Cavalry Archers for raids, and Skirmishers or Ghulams against archers, with a third Town Center to use the bigger villager discount.

First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 2 villagers build a Lumber Camp on the closest woodline and chop
Villager 9 builds a House, then lures the first boar
Villager 10 builds a Mill on the berries and gathers there
Once all sheep are found, push 2 or 3 deer towards the Town Center with the scout
Next 6 villagers on sheep, boar and deer; bring in the second boar when the first runs low
Next 2 villagers go to wood (4 on wood)
Research Loom if you are short of 500 food, then click up to the Feudal Age with 18 villagers plus the scout, usually 10 to 20 seconds earlier than other civilizations
During the age up, move 4 or 5 hunters to wood (8 to 9 on wood) and 4 to the berries
At about 60 percent of the age up, one food villager builds a Barracks
Feudal Age arrives: two villagers build a Stable towards the enemy; train Scout Cavalry nonstop
Next 3 villagers to food: start Farms around the Town Center as the hunt runs out
Research Double-Bit Axe; add Horse Collar once you have 6 or more Farms
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold and mine; research Bloodlines once you have 5 or 6 scouts
Keep adding Farms until about 12; build a Blacksmith with a wood villager
Put 3 more villagers on gold (6 on gold) to prepare the Castle Age
Click up to the Castle Age with 800 food and 200 gold, usually at 30 to 34 villagers

after_feudal: Use the scouts to kill the enemy scout, hit villagers at the woodline and gold, and knock down Houses with your team bonus. Stop when Spearmen and walls are up, and keep the scouts at home to protect your Farms. In Castle Age, choose by what the opponent makes: Camel Riders against Knights and Steppe Lancers, Light Cavalry and Cavalry Archers to keep raiding, Skirmishers or Ghulams against archers. Add a third and fourth Town Center as soon as you are safe, because villagers now cost 18 percent less.
tips: The villager discount means you float a bit more food than usual; spend it on an extra scout or start Farms earlier.
Scouts with the team bonus knock down Houses and camps quickly, so pick those targets when the villagers garrison.
Bloodlines and Forging matter more for you, since camels and Light Cavalry carry your army until the Imperial Age.
Camel Riders are melee units that die quickly under towers and Castles; send siege or Bombard Cannons at buildings instead.
beaten_by: Early Spearmen and a quick wall stop the scouts and leave you with an expensive Stable army. Men-at-Arms into archers is also hard, because scouts lose to both. Switch to an Archery Range when you see Spearmen, or go home and take a faster Castle Age. In Castle Age, massed Crossbowmen beat Camel Riders, so answer them with Skirmishers, Light Cavalry and Ghulams.

title: Huns Fast Castle into Cavalry Archers
summary: Skip Houses, reach the Castle Age early and mass discounted Cavalry Archers from two or three Archery Ranges before the opponent has Skirmishers or Camels out.
description:
A standard 27 villager Fast Castle with the Hun bonuses worked in. No Houses means the wood that other civilizations spend on housing goes into Lumber Camps, the Mill and your first farms, and you never lose production time to being housed.

Your two Feudal Age buildings are the Archery Range and the Blacksmith, since both lead to the Cavalry Archer plan. In the Castle Age Cavalry Archers cost 10% less for the Huns, so two Archery Ranges plus a third shortly after are affordable on a normal economy.

Cavalry Archers need upgrades before they fight well. Plan on Thumb Ring, Fletching and Bloodlines in the first few minutes of the Castle Age and move out with 10 to 12 units. This build takes practice to control, which is why it is rated advanced.
