Click up to the Castle Age with 29 villagers plus the scout as soon as both buildings are done
During the age up, add farms with new villagers and get Horse Collar
Castle Age: build a second Archery Range, start Cavalry Archers and research Thumb Ring
Fletching at the Blacksmith and Bloodlines at a Stable; add a third range when wood allows
New villagers mostly to gold and farms; aim for 8 to 10 on gold

after_feudal:
Move out with 10 to 12 Cavalry Archers once Thumb Ring and Fletching are in. Shoot at villagers on wood and gold, run from Skirmishers and Camels, and never stop production. Add a Town Center or two behind the pressure once your army controls the map.

Get Husbandry, Ballistics, Bodkin Arrow and Parthian Tactics as the game goes on. If the opponent masses Skirmishers, research Marauders or build Stables for Knights and Tarkans; if they mass Camels or Knights, stay on Cavalry Archers and add a few Pikemen at home.
tips: Cavalry Archers miss moving targets without Ballistics and Thumb Ring; buy them early.
Hit and run: stop, shoot, then move before melee units connect.
Keep the scout alive and use it to check for Skirmishers before you commit.
A forward Archery Range cuts walking time, but keep it out of reach of enemy towers.
beaten_by: An early Feudal rush punishes any Fast Castle, and the Huns have no House walls to slow it. Keep a few villagers ready to palisade and fight under the Town Center. In the Castle Age, Elite Skirmishers and Camel Riders are the counters to Cavalry Archers; switch to Knights against Skirmishers and keep kiting Camels. A fast Knight rush from a civilization with strong Knights can also hurt before you have numbers, so add Pikemen at home if you scout it.

In return you never build a House, so the three starting villagers go to the sheep at once and the villager who would build Houses gathers instead. The Mill comes with the forager once your woodcutters have brought in 100 wood.

In the Feudal Age your Stable trains Scout Cavalry 20% faster than other civilizations', so a single Stable keeps up a steady stream and a second Stable gives you a very large Feudal army. Scout early with the Scout Cavalry and decide whether to keep raiding, add a second Stable, or go up to Knights or Cavalry Archers.

Click up to the Castle Age once you have 25 or more villagers on food and wood and some gold mining. Against archer civilizations make Knights from two or three Stables. Against infantry or Spearmen add Archery Ranges and switch to Cavalry Archers, which cost 10% less in the Castle Age. Thumb Ring, Bloodlines and Husbandry are the first upgrades either way.

Hit the woodline first; berry villagers sit next to the Mill and are easier to defend.

title: Inca Instant Champi Drush
summary: Spend the starting wood on a House and a Barracks at once, send four or five Champi Scouts at the opponent in the Dark Age and keep booming behind it with a Settlement on berries.
description:
The Inca have no Militia, but the Champi Scout trains at the Barracks in the Dark Age and works as a fast drush unit. It has 2 pierce armor, a bonus against Scout Cavalry and costs 50 food and 25 gold, 15% less food for the Inca in the Dark Age. Your 100 starting gold pays for four of them without any gold mining.

The build puts the Barracks down with the starting villagers. Two of them build a House (which holds 10 population for the Inca) and one builds the Barracks with the rest of the starting wood. The Barracks counts as your second Dark Age building, so the Settlement you build later at the berries is not needed for the Feudal requirement.

Wood comes from straggler trees next to the Town Center at first, since the Inca have no Lumber Camp. Champi Scouts train slowly, about 42 seconds each, so keep the Barracks busy from the moment it finishes. The goal is to slow down the opponent's walls and kill a few villagers, while your economy keeps going at home. Morley Games recorded this opening right after The Last Chieftains came out; the Champi Scout has since lost some attack and speed, so expect fewer kills and more disruption than in that video.

Your starting Champi Scout looks for sheep; bring the free Llama to the Town Center as extra food
First 6 villagers on sheep (the builders join them when they finish)
Barracks done: train a Champi Scout; it scouts for the rest of the sheep while the starting one finds the opponent
Villager 7 lures the first boar

Next 2 villagers also on straggler trees (6 on wood); one of them builds a second House around 12 or 13 population

An existing villager lures the second boar; the next 2 new villagers go on boar
Next 3 villagers build a Settlement next to the berries and forage; move 3 villagers from the boar to the berries (6 on berries)
Send the Champi Scouts in as one group: hit woodcutters and builders, and use Outposts or blocking to slow walls
Next 4 villagers to wood (8 on wood). If the gold is close to a drop site, put 2 on gold and only 2 more on wood
Build a Settlement at the main woodline once the straggler trees run out; it also adds 10 population
Research Loom and keep seeding Farms around the Town Center as the sheep and boar run out
Click up to the Feudal Age around 22 to 24 villagers
During the age up, add villagers to gold (3 or 4 in total) for the Champi Runner upgrade or archers

after_feudal:
Decide on the follow up before you click up. For Feudal pressure, research the Champi Runner upgrade at the Barracks (90 food and 60 gold), build an Archery Range and add archers or Skirmishers to the surviving Champis. For a faster Castle Age, wall the berries and wood, get Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar, and click up with about 28 villagers for Kamayuks and Slingers.

In either case keep your Champi Scouts alive. They stay useful as scouts and as a quick reaction force against enemy Scout Cavalry, which they beat thanks to their bonus damage.
tips: A Settlement counts as two buildings for the Feudal requirement, so in Inca builds without a Barracks one Settlement is enough to click up.
Do not send the Champis one at a time. Four or five together kill villagers without Loom quickly.
Villagers with Loom can beat a Champi in a fight. If the opponent pulls 6 or more villagers at your Champis, run.
Use the second Champi Scout to find all sheep while the first one finds the opponent.
One House or Settlement holds 10 population, so check your population cap less often than with other civilizations.
beaten_by: Early walls and quick Loom are the main answers. If the opponent walls before your Champis arrive, use them to block walling villagers or build an Outpost for vision, then go home and play a normal Feudal game. Feudal archers need many shots to kill Champis because of their pierce armor, but Men-at-Arms and Spearmen in numbers beat them. Against a Men-at-Arms response, get the Champi Runner upgrade and Slingers later in the Castle Age.

title: Italians Archers (21 pop, two ranges)
summary: A two range archer opening that uses the cheaper Feudal Age to click up with 20 villagers. Italian Archers have an extra point of melee and pierce armor, so they win even archer fights and survive Town Center fire better.

Pick it on open maps against civilizations that do not have a big Skirmisher bonus. It also transitions smoothly into the Italian Castle Age: Crossbowmen with armor, cheap University upgrades and a cheaper Castle Age click. title: Italians Water Fast Feudal Galleys (26 pop)
summary: A full water opening for maps where the sea decides the game. Cheaper Fishing Ships and a cheaper Feudal Age let you fight for the water a little earlier, and every Dock upgrade after that costs a quarter less.
description:
On water maps the player who wins the first ship fights takes the fish and pins the other player in their base. The Italians start that fight with three small advantages: Fishing Ships cost about 64 wood instead of 75, the Feudal Age costs 425 food, and every Dock technology, including Gillnets, Careening and the War Galley upgrade, costs 25 percent less.

The build makes Fishing Ships early and nonstop from a first Dock built around villager 12, clicks up with about 20 villagers and five or six Fishing Ships, and builds two more Docks during the age up. In the Feudal Age, all three Docks make warships. Use it on maps with lots of deep fish and a shared sea, like Islands, Team Islands, Baltic or Four Lakes. On a hybrid map with a land route, add a Barracks and a few Archers or Skirmishers in case of a land rush. F1ReAoE's 2026 video on Migration shows this kind of opening with the Italians.

First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop
Villager 11 lures the first boar

Make Fishing Ships from the Dock whenever you have 64 wood, nonstop until you have 5 or 6

Next 6 villagers on sheep and boar; lure the second boar
Click up to the Feudal Age with 20 villagers, 5 Fishing Ships and the scout once you have 425 food; skip Loom
During the age up, move food villagers to a second Lumber Camp (12 to 14 on wood) and 4 to gold
The builder places a second Dock towards the enemy side of the water and a Barracks on land
Feudal Age arrives: research Double-Bit Axe and start warships from both Docks, Fire Galleys if the enemy has Fire Galleys, otherwise Galleys
Build a third Dock and keep all three producing
Research Gillnets at the Dock once the warship production is steady; it costs you a quarter less
New villagers go to gold until 7 or 8 are mining, then to Farms; make 1 or 2 more Fishing Ships if your fish are safe
Build a Blacksmith for Fletching, which also boosts Galleys, and a Market for the Castle Age

after_feudal: Win the first fights with ships grouped together, then push to the enemy Docks and fish. Keep Fishing Ships safe behind your warships, and replace lost ones right away; they are cheap for you. Click up to the Castle Age with about 30 villagers and 8 Fishing Ships; you only need 680 food and 170 gold. In the Castle Age, research War Galley and Careening, both discounted, and add Fire Ships or Demolition Ships against massed Galleys. In the Imperial Age, Galleons and Cannon Galleons with the gunpowder discount finish the water, and Condottieri in Transport Ships are a strong landing force.
tips: Fishing Ships at about 64 wood mean five ships for the price of a bit more than four. Make them nonstop early.
Group warships with a control group and fight with all of them at once; ships arriving one by one lose.
Fire Galleys beat Galleys, Galleys beat Demolition Rafts, and Demolition Rafts beat clumped Fire Galleys. Scout what the enemy makes.
Fletching and Bodkin Arrow at the Blacksmith add attack to your Galleys.
Keep a Barracks or a few towers at home on hybrid maps. Losing the land war while winning the water is a common way to lose.
beaten_by: A faster Fire Galley opening from a civilization with a naval bonus can take the water before your third Dock is up. If that happens, pull Fishing Ships back, build a tower near your shore and fight again once you have more Docks. On hybrid maps, a land rush with Scout Cavalry or Archers can hit while your wood goes into ships. Scout the land route and keep a Barracks ready.

title: Japanese Men-at-Arms into Archers (20 pop)
summary: Three Militia during the age up become fast-attacking Men-at-Arms on arrival, and the 50 wood drop sites leave enough wood for an Archery Range right behind them.

Use it on open maps when you want to take control in Feudal. St4rk's version aims to finish games around the 11 to 12 minute mark; the build below is a little more relaxed and works as a starting point.

title: Jurchens Fast Castle Steppe Lancers (21+2)
summary: A fast Castle Age into Steppe Lancers that attack 25% faster. Meat that never decays lets you live on sheep, boar and deer longer and click Castle Age at about 13:40 with only six Farms.
description:
Jurchen mounted units attack 25% faster from the Feudal Age, which makes their Steppe Lancers almost as strong in a rush as the Mongol ones. Morley Games built this opening around that: reach the Castle Age at about 13:40, start Steppe Lancers from one Stable, break through the enemy Feudal army and raid.

The other bonus that matters is that meat from hunted and herded animals never decays. You can shoot deer as soon as they are under the Town Center and eat them later, and you can spread villagers over several carcasses without losing food. That saves Farms in the Feudal Age and gets you up faster.

Play it on open maps against opponents who are not committed to early Men-at-Arms. Against a Men-at-Arms player, take Loom and build a tower at your gold.

Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build a Stable and a Blacksmith; consider a tower at your gold
Next 2 villagers go to gold (4 on gold)
Move 4 meat villagers to berries (6 on berries); the rest start Farms as the meat runs out, about 6 Farms
Click up to the Castle Age with 23 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold; force drop food if you are short
Just past halfway through the age up, research Bloodlines so it lands with the Castle Age
Castle Age arrives: train Steppe Lancers nonstop; next 3 villagers go to Farms and 1 to gold (5 on gold)

after_feudal:
Five gold miners keep one Stable busy. Send the first three or four Steppe Lancers to kill the enemy's Feudal army or Scouts, then go for villagers; by 17 minutes you should be raiding inside the enemy base. Keep adding Farms and villagers, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar when the wood allows, and add a second Stable once you have eight gold miners.

A forward Siege Workshop with Rocket Carts makes the push much stronger against Spearmen and archers, and Siege Engineers is cheap for you. Later, add Town Centers behind the raids and move into Grenadiers and siege for the late game.
tips: Steppe Lancers attack from slightly out of melee range, so they can fight in a tight group behind each other.
Six villagers on one carcass and four on another spreads the food better than five and five.
Get Bloodlines before you fight archers; it is the upgrade that keeps Lancers alive.
Avoid Pikemen and Camels; raid somewhere else when they show up.
beaten_by: Men-at-Arms in the Feudal Age are the biggest danger, because the build has few military units before Castle Age. A tower at gold, Loom and a few Spearmen from your Barracks handle them. Pikemen and Camel Riders beat Steppe Lancers in Castle Age, and a walled opponent with Crossbowmen and towers can stall the raid. If the Lancers cannot get in, switch to Rocket Carts, Grenadiers and a boom.

summary: A 19 pop Scout Cavalry opening that moves the sheep villagers onto Pastures instead of Farms and gets Forging in place of Bloodlines. Khitan scouts train 15% faster and gain +2 attack from Forging.
description:
This is the Khitans' standard open map start. The Dark Age is a normal 19 pop scout build. The changes come when the sheep run out: you build Pastures for two villagers each instead of Farms, and you do not need the Mill for them. Keep the Mill on the berries anyway, since berries are faster food early on.

In the Feudal Age your scouts train 15% faster. The Khitans have no Bloodlines, but Forging gives their melee units +2 attack instead of +1, so it is the upgrade that wins scout fights and kills villagers faster. Get it early. Domestication at the Mill replaces Horse Collar and adds an animal to every new Pasture.

The scouts lead into a strong Castle Age. With Iron Casting your melee units have +4 attack, so Steppe Lancers become a hard-hitting raid unit, and the half-price Heavy Cavalry Archer upgrade is ready as soon as you arrive.

First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood

Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar under the Town Center

Pastures need no Mill; place them close to the Town Center so herders can hide in it
Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build a Stable
Make Scout Cavalry nonstop; they train 15% faster than other civilizations' scouts
Research Double-Bit Axe, then build a Blacksmith and research Forging (+2 attack for Khitans)
New villagers to wood until about 10, so you can keep building and rebuilding Pastures
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Research Domestication at the Mill when food allows; it adds an animal to new Pastures
Click up to the Castle Age at about 28 to 30 villagers

after_feudal:
Raid with scouts in a group, kill villagers and avoid Spearmen. With Forging your scouts beat most Feudal scouts and can fight Skirmishers well.

In the Castle Age, research Iron Casting. Then choose: Steppe Lancers from the Stable are the strongest raiders and beat archers, while Heavy Cavalry Archers, available now at half price, are hard to catch and good against slow armies. Add Skirmishers and Pikemen from fast-training buildings to defend. Build one or two more Town Centers and Pastures next to them, and research Pastoralism when your food economy is big enough.
tips: Pastures take two villagers each; move sheep villagers in pairs so nobody waits.
A Pasture starts with 345 food for two villagers, about the same per villager as a Farm. Watch for dead Pastures and rebuild them quickly.
Forging is your Bloodlines. Research it before fighting another scout army.
The team bonus gives your own infantry +2 attack against archers, so a few Spearmen also trade decently with archers.
Keep the Mill on berries; Pastures do not replace berries in the Dark Age.
beaten_by: A walled archer opening holds the scouts and forces you to the Castle Age with less damage done; switch to Skirmishers and go up. Camel and Scout Cavalry civilizations with Bloodlines can beat your scouts before Forging, so delay fights until you have it. Raids on your Pastures hurt, since each one has two villagers; keep a few Spearmen at home and build Pastures close to the Town Center.

title: Khmer Fast Castle into Knights or Elephants (25+2)
summary: The Khmer skip both Feudal Age buildings and click the Castle Age as soon as they have the resources, landing a Knight or Battle Elephant push a minute or more before most fast Castle builds.
description:
Every other civilization needs two Feudal Age buildings, usually a Blacksmith and a Market or Stable, before it can click the Castle Age. The Khmer need none, so this build reaches the Feudal Age with 25 villagers, makes two more, and clicks up again the moment 800 food and 200 gold are in the bank. The wood that would have gone into those buildings goes into Farms and the first Stables instead.

The Farms are the other Khmer advantage here. Farmers drop food straight into the stockpile, so you can place Farms anywhere, and some players skip the berries entirely and farm around the Town Center from the start. That is slower but much harder to raid; the version below uses berries, which is the more common choice.

In the Castle Age, Knights are the simple follow-up. Battle Elephants with Husbandry and Tusk Swords are the stronger push against civilizations that lack good camels or Halberdiers. Either way, get two Stables down during the Castle age up.

Next 2 villagers on boar or sheep
As the sheep run out, put those villagers on Farms. Khmer Farms need no drop site, so place them where your Town Center can protect them
Next 4 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (8 on wood)

Build two Stables during the age up; the Khmer can place them without a Barracks
New villagers go to gold; move the berry villagers to gold and Farms when the bushes run out

A clean run lands in the Castle Age around 14:00, about a minute ahead of a normal fast Castle. Leaner versions with fewer Dark Age villagers reach it before 13:00. Start Knights or Battle Elephants from both Stables at once

Send most new villagers to gold; Battle Elephants cost 100 food and 70 gold, so a two Stable elephant push needs more food than a Knight push. Research Bloodlines and Husbandry first, then Tusk Swords if you went elephants. Raid together, kill villagers, and add a second and third Town Center behind the attack, using the Farms-anywhere bonus to spread your farms around each new Town Center. If the opponent walls up and makes Halberdiers or camels, switch to Crossbowmen, Scorpions or Ballista Elephants from a Castle.
tips: Because you skip the Feudal buildings, you have no Barracks or Archery Range. Wall your woodline and gold before you click to the Castle Age.
Build Houses next to the woodline and gold; villagers can hide inside them if the opponent raids during the age up.
If the opponent opens with a strong Feudal rush, build the Archery Range or Barracks you skipped and make Skirmishers or Spearmen. The build still works a minute later.
Battle Elephants are slow without Husbandry. Get it before the first raid.
beaten_by: Fast Archers or Scout Cavalry on an open map can catch you in the Feudal Age with no army and no production building. In the Castle Age, Monks, Camel Riders and massed Pikemen stop elephants, and the Khmer have no Heresy. Against those, switch the Stables to Hussars and add Scorpions or Crossbowmen.

summary: A fast Khmer scout rush: no Barracks, no Mill before the Feudal Age, click up at 18 population and put the Stable down the moment the age lands.
description:
The Khmer need no buildings to advance or to unlock other buildings, so this scout rush cuts everything that does not help the first Scout Cavalry. There is no Barracks, which saves 175 wood, and no Mill until the Feudal Age, which lets you click up with only a Lumber Camp. The food comes from sheep and both boars, so you do not need to push deer, and the build works on maps with chickens too.

You still have to wait for the Feudal Age to build the Stable. The age up is the moment to prepare: move villagers to wood so you have 175 wood waiting, and put the Stable next to your woodline or toward the opponent.

The cost of the build is a thin economy and no Barracks for Spearmen. Against a player who walls quickly or opens with Archers, plan to add an Archery Range for Skirmishers or go up to the Castle Age soon.

title: Koreans Archers (21 pop)
summary: A two range archer rush that clicks up with 20 villagers. Korean archers cost about half the wood and get their armor upgrades for free, so you need fewer lumberjacks and more gold miners than other civilizations.
description:
This is a standard two range archer opening adjusted for the Korean bonuses. Archers and Skirmishers cost 50 percent less wood, so after the two Archery Ranges are built your wood need drops sharply and most new villagers go to gold and food. The archer armor technologies are free, so your first Blacksmith money goes into Fletching.

Play it on Arabia and other open maps. The archers take map control, kill the enemy scout and villagers at the woodline, and they trade well in archer mirrors because of the free armor. Against a Scout Cavalry opening, add a few cheap Spearmen at home.

The usual follow up is a third Archery Range, then Castle Age Crossbowmen with Thumb Ring, Rocket Carts against Skirmishers and a Castle for War Wagons. You can also add a second Town Center in Castle Age if the archers have done enough damage.

Click up to the Castle Age at about 30 to 35 villagers while the archers keep the opponent busy. In Castle Age, upgrade to Crossbowmen, research Bodkin Arrow and Thumb Ring, and build a Siege Workshop for Rocket Carts, which beat Skirmishers and infantry. Add Pikemen or Fire Lancers against cavalry and a Castle for War Wagons or Eupseong if you need to defend. A second and third Town Center go down once the map is under control.
tips: With the wood discount you can afford archers and Farms at the same time; do not overbuild Lumber Camps.
Your archers already have armor, so they beat even numbers of enemy archers early in Feudal; take those fights.
Spearmen cost almost no wood for you, so a few at home stop Scout Cavalry cheaply.
If your opponent goes Skirmishers, add a couple of Men-at-Arms or Spearmen and keep shooting villagers.
beaten_by: Skirmishers with scouts or Men-at-Arms and a wall at home are the standard answer, and a Scout Cavalry opening punishes archers that leave the base empty. A fast Castle Knight push also arrives before Rocket Carts and Pikemen are ready if you overspend on archers. Mix in Spearmen against cavalry and get to Castle Age on time.

title: Koreans Tower Rush (19 pop)
summary: A 19 pop Feudal tower rush that uses faster Korean stone miners and free tower upgrades, backed by cheap Archers to deny the enemy wood and gold.
description:
The tower rush is an old Korean specialty. Korean stone miners work 20 percent faster, and every Watch Tower upgrade is free, so your towers become Guard Towers the moment you reach Castle Age. You start with 200 stone, enough for the first tower, and four or five stone miners pay for more.

The idea is to send several villagers to the enemy base during the age up, hide them near the enemy woodline or gold, and build a tower the second Feudal Age lands. Each new tower goes in range of the last one, moving toward the next resource, until the opponent has nowhere safe to gather. Cheap Korean archers from a forward Archery Range kill the villagers who try to build or fight around your towers.

This is a gamble on reaction speed. Against a player who scouts you and builds a Barracks or towers of their own, it fails, and you will be far behind. Use it now and then, on open maps with resources close to the enemy Town Center. Hera's own video on this build points out that tower rushing teaches you little about the rest of the game.

First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 2 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 9 lures the first boar
Villager 10 goes to the boar
Next 2 villagers build a Mill on the berries and gather there
Next 6 villagers on sheep and boar; a hunter lures the second boar
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age with 18 villagers plus the scout
Move 4 food villagers to the enemy base and hide them out of sight near their woodline or gold
Move 3 food villagers to stone and build a Mining Camp; add 2 villagers to wood (4 on wood)
Feudal Age arrives: the forward villagers build the first Watch Tower right away, on the edge of the enemy woodline or gold
New villagers go to stone until 5 are mining, then to berries and Farms
Build the second tower in range of the first; wall the builders with palisades if enemy villagers come to fight
One forward villager builds an Archery Range; Korean Archers cost little wood, so make them nonstop
Keep stepping towers towards the next resource; garrison a villager in a tower under attack to add an arrow
Once the opponent is pinned, add Farms at home and click Castle Age; your towers become Guard Towers for free

after_feudal: When the rush works, the opponent loses wood and gold and falls into a long Feudal Age. Keep the Archery Range working, add a Blacksmith for Fletching, and click Castle Age while they rebuild. Your towers upgrade to Guard Towers on arrival, and Eupseong at a Castle gives them +2 range. A forward Castle near the enemy base finishes the job. If the rush fails, pull the villagers home, make Archers and Spearmen and go for a normal Castle Age.
tips: Place towers on the far side of resources first so enemy villagers cannot just move to the other half.
Bring at least four villagers forward; one builder gets killed or chased away too easily.
Watch for a forward Barracks: Men-at-Arms or Spearmen kill your builders before the tower finishes.
Each Watch Tower needs 35 wood as well as the 125 stone, so keep a little wood in the bank.
beaten_by: Fast reactions: scouting your forward villagers, pulling villagers to attack the builders before the tower finishes, and walling the resources you aim for. Men-at-Arms or Spearmen from a quick Barracks kill tower builders, and opponents who build their own towers next to yours trade well because they are close to home. A fast Castle Age with Mangonels, Bombard Cannons or Rams undoes the whole investment.

title: Lithuanians Fast Castle Knights and Monks
summary: Reach the Castle Age early, make Knights from one Stable and send Monks for the Relics so that every Knight hits harder. Then boom behind the army.
description:
Morley Games built this plan around the Lithuanian Relic bonus: a Fast Castle into Knights from one Stable, plus a Monastery straight away. The Knights control the map while Monks collect Relics, and each Relic in your Monastery gives your Knights +1 attack, up to +4. The Monks can also convert villagers or enemy Knights when you attack, and they help you break walls by converting the units behind them.

The extra 100 starting food means the Dark Age needs a little less food than a generic Fast Castle, so you can put that villager on wood or click up one villager earlier. Monasteries work 20% faster for Lithuanians, which shortens the Monk production in the opening minutes of the Castle Age.

You do not need a full wall; the main goal is to protect villagers on their resources and to keep the Knights active.

Train 2 to 3 Monks and send them for the nearest Relics with a Knight escort

after_feudal:
Hit with the first four or five Knights and keep them close enough to protect the Monks. Bring Relics home, and use a Monk or two in fights to convert villagers or enemy Knights. Add Bloodlines, Husbandry and Forging, then a second Town Center and more farms.

If the opponent makes Camels or Halberdiers, use Monks and a few Skirmishers against them. Against Crossbowmen, more Knights with Relic attack trade very well. Click up to the Imperial Age once your economy is at 80 or more villagers and go Paladins, Winged Hussars and Halberdiers.
tips: Four Relics give your Knights +4 attack; that is worth fighting for early.
Keep Monks behind the Knights; one Light Cavalry can kill an unescorted Monk.
Hill Forts is a good buy if the opponent raids your Town Centers with Knights.
Do not wait for many Knights before moving out; early pressure buys time for the Monks.
beaten_by: Feudal Age aggression is the usual problem for any Fast Castle. Palisade around the woodlines and keep villagers ready to fight under the Town Center against Scout Cavalry or Men-at-Arms. In the Castle Age, Camels, Halberdiers and enemy Monks beat Knights; take Relics anyway and mix in Skirmishers or Crossbowmen. An opponent who takes the Relics first removes your bonus, so check where they are with the scout during the Feudal Age.

summary: A food heavy 19 population scout opening that uses the cheaper Scout Cavalry and the free Forging to raid hard the moment Feudal Age arrives.

Villagers kill wolves in one hit for Magyars, so wolves near your woodline or on the way to a forward Stable are no danger. If you play this for the first time, add one more villager on berries and click at 20 population; the build stays the same otherwise.

summary: A Fast Castle that uses both fast Malay age ups to reach the Castle Age a minute early, then floods the map with Battle Elephants that cost a quarter less.

Elephants are slow, so the attack works best on a base that is close or reachable without a long walk past walls and towers. Bring a few villagers to build a forward Stable or a Castle if the map is large.

title: Mapuche Champi Runner Rush (20 pop)
summary: The South American version of a Men-at-Arms rush: three Champi Scouts made during the Feudal Age up become Champi Runners on arrival, with Skirmishers from a Settlement joining them.
description:
The Mapuche have no Militia line; their Barracks trains the Champi Scout, which upgrades to the Champi Runner in the Feudal Age. Champi units are fast and resist arrows, so a small group pins villagers, stops walls and kills straggler woodcutters. Morley Games presented this as the easy first build for the South American civilizations, played here with the Mapuche.

Two Mapuche bonuses fit the build. Foragers drop off 25% more food, so the five berry villagers carry a big part of the Feudal Age food. And Settlements can train Skirmishers, so you can add ranged support without an Archery Range, although they train slowly in the Feudal Age.

The Settlement replaces the Mill, Lumber Camp and Mining Camp. It costs 125 wood, gives 5 population and counts as two buildings for the Feudal Age, so two Settlements and two Houses give you all the population you need for this build.

From here, the usual Mapuche plan is a Castle Age switch into Bolas Riders from two Archery Ranges, with Pikemen and Skirmishers from Settlements as support. If the opponent goes heavy infantry, add Slingers in the Castle Age.

summary: A fast Castle Age that leans on the Mapuche berry bonus and goes straight into Bolas Riders from two Archery Ranges. Ballistics and Fletching early make the Bolas hit what they aim at.

The Bolas Rider is the unit most Mapuche players build in the Castle Age. It replaces the Cavalry Archer, costs less, is much more accurate and needs only the archer Blacksmith upgrades, since it has no Bloodlines or Thumb Ring to research. Every 30 seconds it throws a charged shot that slows the target.

This build gets there quickly. Foragers drop off 25% more food, so you put more villagers on berries than usual and build a Settlement next to them early. LegendaryAoE2 plays it at 23 population with Loom and clicks the Castle Age two villagers later, with a Blacksmith and an Archery Range as the two Feudal buildings.

It works best against opponents who wall and boom, and on maps with many berry patches.

title: Maya Archers (22 pop)
summary: A two-range archer opening with the Maya start: four villagers, an Eagle Scout and Loom while you wait for the first House. Feudal archers are 10% cheaper for the Maya, and your resources last 15% longer.
description:
The Maya are one of the best archer civilizations in the Feudal Age. This build clicks the Feudal Age at 22 pop, 21 villagers plus the Eagle Scout, which puts you on the same timing as a generic 21 pop archer opening but with an extra villager.

You start housed, because four villagers and the Eagle Scout already fill the Town Center's five population. Two villagers on each of the first two Houses get you unhoused quickly, and since the Town Center has nothing to train in the meantime, research Loom right at the start. You will not need to stop for Loom later.

The Eagle Scout is slower than a Scout Cavalry but tougher. Use it to find sheep and scout the opponent. In the Feudal Age, two Archery Ranges produce archers nonstop, and half-price walls keep your economy safe. Follow up with Crossbowmen in the Castle Age, where the discount grows to 20%.

Move 2 food villagers to gold (4 on gold)

Build a Blacksmith and research Fletching; Horse Collar when food allows
Click up to the Castle Age at about 30 to 32 villagers while the archers keep pressure

after_feudal:
Attack with your first five or six archers. Target villagers on wood and gold and kill the opponent's Scout Cavalry or Skirmishers when they are alone. Keep the archers together and retreat from Skirmishers in large numbers or Men-at-Arms you cannot outrun.

In the Castle Age, research Crossbowman, Bodkin Arrow and Bow Saw, and add a third Archery Range. Make Eagle Warriors from the Barracks if the opponent goes Knights or Skirmishers. Add Town Centers behind your walls when you are safe. Once you have a Castle, Plumed Archers and Hul'che Javelineers are both strong additions.

Your resources last 15% longer, so one Lumber Camp lasts a bit longer than usual before you need to move.
Use the Eagle Scout to look for the opponent's buildings early; it survives scout harassment better than a Scout Cavalry.
Walls cost half for you. A full palisade around your wood and gold is cheap insurance.

title: Maya Eagle Scouts and Archers (20 pop)
summary: A Mesoamerican Feudal opening that makes Eagle Scouts from the Barracks and archers from an Archery Range at the same time. Eagles beat Skirmishers, Spearmen and Scout Cavalry, and the archers cover their weakness to Men-at-Arms.

They are strong against the usual answers to archers, which are Skirmishers and Spearmen, and they handle Scout Cavalry. The weakness is Men-at-Arms and archers in numbers, so this build pairs them with archers from one Archery Range.

title: Mongols Scouts with Hunt (18 pop)
summary: The classic Mongol scout rush: both boars early, deer pushed to the Town Center, and a Feudal Age click at 18 population for Scout Cavalry well before most opponents expect them.
description:
Mongol hunters work 40% faster, so boars and deer feed the Town Center with fewer villagers than any other civilization needs. This build leans on that. The 7th villager lures a boar, the scout pushes deer to the Town Center once the sheep are found, and you click up at 18 population, two to four villagers earlier than a normal scout rush. HumzaCrumza's well-known Mongol version goes up at 16 population; 18 is easier to execute and keeps the economy healthier.

On maps where chickens appear instead of deer, the scout cannot push them and they cannot be funnelled into the Town Center. Build the Mill next to the chickens and send the extra food villagers there. The hunt bonus still applies, so the build works with a slightly later click.

The scouts themselves have no Feudal Age bonus, so use the early timing to kill villagers and take map control before the opponent has Spearmen. Mongol Scout Cavalry get their extra hit points only from the Castle Age on.

Research Double-Bit Axe
New villagers go to wood until you have 10, then to berries; build a second Lumber Camp when you can afford it
Research Horse Collar and seed Farms as the hunt under the Town Center runs out

after_feudal: Send the first three or four Scout Cavalry together at the enemy woodline or gold and keep them alive; a Mongol scout rush loses its value if the scouts die to a couple of Spearmen. Keep adding scouts up to six or eight, get Bloodlines, and use them to deny the opponent's deer and forward buildings. Then move to the Castle Age. Cavalry Archers with Thumb Ring or Steppe Lancers are the usual follow-ups, and the Scout Cavalry upgrade to Light Cavalry with 20% more hit points in the Castle Age, which makes them good Monk and siege hunters.
tips: Lure the boar with villager 7; Mongols eat it so quickly that a late boar wastes the bonus.
Push deer only after every sheep is home, and keep the scout busy with them until the Feudal click.
On chicken maps, plan the Mill next to the chickens and expect to click up one or two villagers later.
Against a player who walls early, cut scouts short and take the faster Castle Age instead.
beaten_by: A quick wall with towers and Spearmen stops the raid, and a Men-at-Arms rush can punish the thin Mongol economy. Archers on a hill near the Town Center are also hard to crack with scouts. If the raid does nothing, stop at five or six scouts and go to the Castle Age with Cavalry Archers.

title: Muisca Champi Runner Rush (17 pop)
summary: The Muisca version of a Men-at-Arms rush: a Barracks in the Dark Age, three Champi Scouts during the age up and the Champi Runner upgrade as soon as Feudal Age lands, with Settlements doing the work of Houses, Mill and Lumber Camp.
description:
The Champi Runner is the Feudal upgrade of the Champi Scout: a fast, arrow resistant infantry raider that fills the Man-at-Arms slot for the South American civilizations. Muisca runners get +1 melee armor in the Feudal Age, and a Settlement heals them by 10 hit points per minute, so a small group can fight, pull back and fight again.

The Dark Age is short. You build a Settlement on wood instead of a Lumber Camp, a Barracks with the next wood and a second Settlement on gold so you can pay for the Champi Scouts. Each Settlement also gives 5 population, so two Houses and two Settlements cover everything up to the Feudal Age. You click up at 17 population and train three Champi Scouts during the age up; together with the starting Champi Scout they become four Champi Runners when the upgrade finishes.

Use the rush on open maps to stop walls, kill villagers at the woodline and gold and force the opponent to spend on Spearmen or towers. Follow it with archers or Skirmishers from an Archery Range, which also get the melee armor bonus, then a cheap Castle Age.

Villager 10 lures the first boar

Villager 14 goes to food; lure the second boar when the first runs low
Next 2 villagers build a second Settlement on gold (skip it if the first one already reaches the gold) and mine
Train three Champi Scouts from the Barracks as food and gold allow
Research Loom if you have spare gold, then click up to the Feudal Age with 16 villagers plus the Champi Scout
During the age up, keep the Town Center making villagers; send 3 to food and start Farms as the sheep run out (Farms need a Settlement or Town Center nearby)
Gather the Champi Scouts and walk them toward the enemy base
Feudal Age arrives: research the Champi Runner upgrade at the Barracks right away
Next 2 villagers to gold (4 on gold), then new villagers to wood and Farms
Build an Archery Range and follow up with Archers, or Skirmishers if the enemy goes archers
Place a Settlement near your berries and gather them; add a Blacksmith once you have 8 Farms
Pull wounded runners back to a Settlement to heal, then send them in again

after_feudal: Raid with the runners as one group: kill villagers at the woodline and gold, chase the enemy scout and hit unfinished walls. When Spearmen, towers or archers show up, pull back to heal and switch production to archers or Skirmishers. With the Castle Age costing only 800 food and 100 gold, you can click up at about 28 to 30 villagers. In Castle Age, go Crossbowmen with Herbalism or Champi Warriors with rams, and add Temple Guards if the opponent turns to cavalry.
tips: Settlements count as Houses; with two Settlements you do not need a third House until about 25 population.
Keep the runners together; one runner alone dies to a few villagers with Loom.
A Settlement built near the enemy base is a forward healing spot, but it costs 84 wood and is easy to lose, so place it with care.
If the opponent walls quickly, aim the runners at the gold and the palisades they are still building.
beaten_by: Archers and towers are the main problems: runners are tough against arrows but still lose to a group of archers behind walls, and a tower on the woodline stops the raid. Early Spearmen with villagers fighting back can trade well against a small group of runners. Against an archer opponent, switch to Skirmishers quickly and take a fast Castle Age.

title: Muisca Fast Castle (25 pop)
summary: A fast Castle Age that uses the half price age up: the Castle Age costs 800 food and only 100 gold, so two gold miners are enough and the rest of the economy goes to food and wood.
description:
The Muisca pay 50 percent less gold to advance, so the Castle Age needs only 100 gold. Most fast Castle builds keep three to five villagers on gold; here two are enough, and the saved villagers go to food so you can click up with fewer villagers or at a better time.

Settlements replace the Lumber Camp, Mill and Mining Camp. One Settlement counts as two buildings for the Feudal Age, and each one adds 5 population, which saves you most of the Dark Age Houses. Place them where they touch two resources when you can, for example a woodline next to gold.

In Castle Age the common follow ups are Crossbowmen with Herbalism, a Monk push with Temple Guards, or extra Town Centers. Pick it on closed maps and on Arabia when you can wall; against an early rush, add a few Skirmishers or Champi units and click up a little later.

after_feudal: For the archer plan, build two Archery Ranges, upgrade to Crossbowmen and research Herbalism at a Castle once you have one; your Crossbowmen take +2 melee armor into every fight against Knights and Champi or Eagle raiders. For the Monk plan, build a Monastery, make Monks and train Temple Guards from the same building to protect them. In both cases put 6 to 8 villagers on gold, and add a second Town Center as soon as the army is out. Remember that the Imperial Age also costs half the gold, so a fast Imperial Age is cheaper for you than for anyone else.
tips: Every Settlement is also a House, so count them when you plan your population.
With only 100 gold needed for Castle Age, sell nothing; your two gold miners cover it.
Place Farms around Settlements as well as around the Town Center to shorten walking.
Settlements heal nearby villagers, so build one in the middle of your Farms if you expect raids.
beaten_by: As with any fast Castle Age, an early Feudal rush that reaches you before your walls are up is the main danger, especially archers on open maps. Without cavalry you also cannot chase raiders, so wall and keep Skirmishers or Pikemen ready. In Castle Age, a Knight push before your Temple Guards or Pikemen are out is hard to hold; keep a few Pikemen at home when you scout a Stable.

title: Persians Fast Castle Knights
summary: A standard Fast Castle into Knights that arrives early thanks to the faster Persian Town Center, with an optional Monastery to convert villagers while the Knights raid.
description:
The villager split is the usual 27 villager Fast Castle, but Persians get there sooner. The Town Center works 5% faster in the Dark Age and 10% faster in the Feudal Age, so villagers, Loom and both age ups finish earlier. The extra 50 food and 50 wood at the start also let you build the second Lumber Camp or the Mill a little earlier without waiting on wood.

Morley Games plays this with a Monastery added in the Castle Age: the Knights, which deal +2 damage to archers, keep the opponent busy while one or two Monks convert villagers. That economic damage on top of the Town Center bonus is hard to come back from.

Wall your villagers on their resources rather than walling the whole base; this build wants to be the one doing the attacking.

title: Poles Scouts into Castle Age Knights
summary: A 21 population scout opening that mines stone in Feudal for the Polish gold bonus, then reaches the Castle Age with two or three Stables, a Castle and Szlachta Privileges for cheap Knights.
description:
The Dark Age is the standard 21 population scout build with one Polish change: the Mill at the berries is a Folwark. It costs the same and supports 5 population, so you can save a House in the Dark Age.

In the Feudal Age you put villagers on stone where other civilizations would mine gold. Polish stone miners produce a third of their stone again as gold, so the stone pile pays for Bloodlines and the Castle Age while you save up for a Castle. Once you reach the Castle Age you start Knights at once, build the Castle with the stone you saved, and research Szlachta Privileges to bring the Knight's gold cost down to 30.

Move your farming to a Folwark next to the Town Center as soon as the berries run low; only Farms next to a Folwark give the instant food.

Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on stone; the stone also gives you gold
Next villagers to Farms around a second Folwark next to the Town Center, plus 2 more on stone
Research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar; Bloodlines costs half the food for you, so get it once you have 5 or 6 scouts
Build a Blacksmith and keep adding Farms by the Folwark; reseed Farms from the Folwark queue
Click up to the Castle Age around 30 villagers
While the age loads, build a second Stable and keep mining stone

Research Szlachta Privileges at the Castle, then add a third Stable

after_feudal:
Raid with scouts while the Feudal economy grows, but stop at about six scouts and invest in Farms and stone. The scouts stay useful as a defense against enemy scouts and to pick off villagers that leave their walls.

In the Castle Age, keep Knights coming from two and then three Stables. After Szlachta Privileges your Knights cost 60 food and 30 gold, so food is the limiting resource; keep adding Farms around Folwarks and get Heavy Plow early. Add a second Town Center with its own Folwark once the first Knight group is out. If the opponent switches to Pikemen or Camel Riders, train Obuchs from the Castle.
tips: Build Farms in a tight ring around each Folwark; only those Farms trigger the instant food.
Put stone miners on the stone pile closest to the Town Center so they can garrison quickly.
Villagers regenerate from the Feudal Age, so pull wounded villagers from a raid instead of letting them die.
Keep 2 or 3 Light Cavalry with the Knights to chase archers and Monks; the upgrades are cheap for you.
If the opponent has many archers in the Castle Age, add a Siege Workshop and a couple of Battering Rams before attacking.

A fast archer opening that hits your stone miners early also slows the Castle, so keep a few scouts at home to defend the stone line.

Research the Long Swordsman upgrade and Chain Mail Armor; train Long Swordsmen from the Barracks
Move out with 6 to 8 Scorpions behind 5 or more Long Swordsmen; add a Battering Ram for buildings

after_feudal: Push toward the opponent's resources with the infantry in front and the Scorpions a few tiles behind. Scorpion bolts pass through every unit in their path, so line up shots on clumps. Keep adding villagers to gold and wood and build a second Town Center when the push is under way. Once you have stone, a Castle unlocks Ballistas, and the Scorpions start firing a third faster. If the opponent goes for Knights, add Pikemen; if they make Mangonels, attack them with Long Swordsmen right away.
tips: Scorpions are wood heavy; keep at least 10 villagers on wood once both workshops are running.
Thanks to the team bonus, Roman Scorpions have a minimum range of 1 and can still shoot units that get close.
Use attack-move with the Scorpions so they stop and shoot at the first enemies that come into range.
Do not walk Scorpions into a Castle or Town Center; use Battering Rams or Trebuchets for buildings.
beaten_by: Knights that reach the Scorpions, Mangonels, and a fast Feudal rush before your walls are up. Keep Pikemen or Long Swordsmen between the Scorpions and the enemy, and attack enemy Mangonels with infantry the moment they show up. Bombard Cannons in the Imperial Age outrange Scorpions, so close that game out before then.

After the first attack you can keep making infantry, add Skirmishers, or click Castle Age for Long Swordsmen and Scorpions.

title: Saracens Archers with Market (20 pop)
summary: A quick archer opening with no Dark Age Mill and two Archery Ranges, plus a 75 wood Market that turns the starting stone into gold for more archers. Saracen archers also deal extra damage to buildings.
description:
This is the Saracen take on the archer rush. The Dark Age follows Tatoh's Tati rush: sheep and boar under the Town Center, three wood villagers, a Mining Camp on gold, and no Mill, since the Lumber Camp and Mining Camp already count as your two buildings. You click up at 20 population and open with two Archery Ranges.

The Saracen part comes in the Feudal Age. Their Market costs only 75 wood and trades at a 5% fee, so selling the 200 starting stone returns almost the full value in gold. That pays for several extra archers and Fletching right when the archers need to move out. St4rk calls archers with a Market his default with this civilization, because it uses the cheap Market, the low fee and the bonus damage Saracen archers deal to buildings, and the Market's line of sight helps defend too.

Unlike the all in Tati rush, this version keeps making villagers and builds a Mill and Farms in the Feudal Age.

First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 10 lures the first boar

Move 3 sheep villagers to gold with a Mining Camp; it is your second Dark Age building, so no Mill is needed
Next 2 villagers on sheep
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age with 19 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, move 6 food villagers to wood (9 on wood) and 1 to gold (4 on gold); a wood villager builds a Barracks halfway through
Feudal Age arrives: wood villagers build two Archery Ranges; start Archers from both
A wood villager builds a Market (75 wood) as soon as you can afford it; sell the 200 starting stone for gold
The next villager builds a Mill on the berries and forages; the remaining food villagers start Farms as the sheep and boar run out
Build a Blacksmith and research Fletching before the archers attack
Next villagers go to gold until 7 are mining, then to Farms; research Double-Bit Axe

after_feudal:
Move out with six to eight Archers once Fletching is done. Shoot villagers at the wood and gold, and use the bonus damage against buildings to knock down palisades, houses and a forward tower. Keep the Market working: sell wood or food you do not need, buy what the ranges are short of, and trade in small steps to keep prices fair.

For the Castle Age, Crossbowmen with Ballistics and Bodkin Arrow are the core. Add a Stable and Camel Riders if Knights appear, since Saracen Camels have 25% more hit points. Monks with Bimaristan and more Town Centers come next. If you want the all in version, Tatoh stops villagers in Feudal, builds a third Archery Range and moves five wood villagers to gold.
tips: Sell the stone 100 at a time and watch the price; stop if it drops too far.
The Market has a large line of sight; place it where it watches a raid path into your base.
Saracen archers deal more damage to houses and palisades, so attack walls that block your archers.
Skip Horse Collar until the Farms are running; the Market can cover a short food gap.
beaten_by: Skirmishers with Padded Archer Armor and a quick wall stop the archers; switch to a Stable with Scouts or go up to the Castle Age with Knights or Camels. A Drush delays the ranges, so wall and keep the first archers at home until the Militia are gone. Scouts that reach unprotected archers punish this build, so keep the group together and add Spearmen if needed.

title: Saxons Archers with Tower (19 pop)
summary: A safe 19 pop archer opening. The stone from your Saxon drop sites pays for a Watch Tower on your gold without any stone mining, archers pressure the opponent, and in the Castle Age you add two Town Centers for a 15% foot soldier discount.
description:
Hera showed this opening when the Saxons came out. You build two Lumber Camps, a Mill and Mining Camps, and each one gives 35 food and 10 stone. That is enough stone for a tower on your gold by the middle of the Feudal Age, without sending a single villager to mine stone. From the Castle Age that tower fires double arrows.

The plan is archers to pressure and to defend, a tower to protect your gold, and a full wall at home. Click the Castle Age around 17:30 while the archers keep the opponent busy, then add two Town Centers right away. With three Town Centers your foot soldiers cost 15% less, and a fourth Town Center or a Castle brings it to 20%.

IdleTC notes that Hera's version was a first look against the AI, so treat the Castle Age follow-up as a starting point. The ladder data so far shows Saxon players leaning on Varangian Guards, Hearth Troops, Spearmen and archers.

Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar under the Town Center

Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries in total); a villager from under the Town Center lures the second boar
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar under the Town Center
Research Loom

Feudal Age arrives: the same two villagers build an Archery Range; then one walls and the other goes to gold. Move 2 villagers from under the Town Center to gold
Research Double-Bit Axe
First new villager to gold (4 on gold); build a Mining Camp on the stone next to the gold for another 10 stone
Make archers nonstop
Build a Watch Tower on your gold with the drop site stone
Research Horse Collar; sheep villagers move to straggler trees, and new villagers go to wood and build Farms
Attack with your first 3 archers and keep adding to the group
Build a Blacksmith and research Fletching; when wood reaches about 15 villagers, move one to gold and start moving wood villagers onto Farms
New villagers: 1 more to gold and 3 to stone for the Castle Age Town Centers
Click up to the Castle Age around 17:30 while the archers keep pressure; research Gold Mining on the way

after_feudal:
Build two Town Centers the moment the Castle Age arrives (three in total, 15% off foot soldiers). Research Crossbowman, Bodkin Arrow and Bow Saw. Then add a fourth Town Center if you are booming or a Castle if the game is tense; either gives the full 20%.

The main Castle Age army is Varangian Guards and Skirmishers from extra Barracks and Archery Ranges. Research Gambesons so the Varangian Guards beat Skirmishers. Your towers now fire double arrows, so fight close to them and garrison archers inside when you are attacked. Later, switch to Hearth Troops and Varangian Guards and research Shield Wall.
tips: Every Mill, Lumber Camp and Mining Camp gives 35 food and 10 stone; build the Mining Camp on stone next to your gold to collect another 10.
Do not mine stone for the Feudal tower; the drop sites pay for it.
The tower is a Castle Age weapon too: from then on it fires two arrows with nobody inside.
Keep the archers alive. They hold your gold and become the Crossbowmen of your Castle Age.
The foot soldier discount only applies once a Town Center or Castle is finished.
beaten_by: A Scout Cavalry rush that reaches your wood before your wall is done can hurt, since you make archers instead of Spearmen; add one or two Spearmen if you see scouts early. A drush or Men-at-Arms delays your Archery Range, so keep the Barracks ready. Against a fast castle, your archers should do real damage before Knights arrive; build Pikemen once you see a Stable.

title: Saxons Fast Castle into Town Centers (26+2)
summary: A fast castle that collects 140 food and 40 stone from Saxon drop sites before the Feudal Age, clicks up one villager earlier than the generic version, and builds two Town Centers on arrival for a 15% discount on every foot soldier.
description:
The Saxon Strategy page on the fandom wiki says their bonuses push them toward a fast castle boom. The drop site food lets you click up a little earlier, the drop site stone adds to your starting 200 stone, and every Town Center you add makes infantry and foot archers 5% cheaper.

This build is the standard fast castle with Saxon numbers. A Mill, two Lumber Camps and a Mining Camp give 140 food and 40 stone in the Dark Age, roughly the food for one more villager, so the build clicks Feudal with 25 villagers instead of 27. The stone you start with covers both Castle Age Town Centers. On open maps, wall before clicking Castle Age.

After three Town Centers, either add a fourth or a Castle for the full 20% discount, and make Varangian Guards, Crossbowmen and Skirmishers. Some players use the extra stone for a Castle drop instead, which also lets you train Hearth Troops early.

Add Barracks and an Archery Range; research Gambesons before making Varangian Guards

after_feudal:
With three Town Centers working, grow to about 50 villagers while you start a Castle Age army. Varangian Guards from two Barracks are the core, with Skirmishers or Crossbowmen from one or two Archery Ranges. Varangian Guards win most even fights and earn gold while fighting. Add Pikemen if the opponent has Knights.

Put towers on your gold and at chokepoints; they fire double arrows from now on. Repairers work faster for you, so fix damaged towers instead of rebuilding them. Click the Imperial Age around 65 to 70 villagers, then research Shield Wall and switch to Hearth Troops if the opponent goes archers.

beaten_by: Feudal aggression before your walls are up, since you have no army until the Castle Age. A Scout or archer rush that reaches your wood can cost more than the boom gains, so wall early and use a tower. In the Castle Age, a fast Knight push or a Monk and siege push can hit before the Town Centers are finished; build one Town Center instead of two if you see the push coming and spend the rest on Pikemen and Skirmishers.

title: Shu Archers (22 pop)
summary: A two Archery Range opening built around the Shu lumberjack bonus: only five villagers on sheep, wood started early, and cheap Fletching for Archers that see further than the opponent's.
description:
Shu lumberjacks bring in 0.7 food for every 10 wood, so wood villagers help pay for the next villager from the start. This build takes advantage of that by putting only five villagers on sheep and sending villagers six to eight to wood, as many Shu players do. The rest is a normal 22 population archer opening: boars and berries carry the Dark Age, you click up with a strong wood economy and two Archery Ranges go down as soon as the Feudal Age lands.

The Shu bonuses keep helping in the Feudal Age. Fletching and the archer armor upgrade at the Blacksmith cost 25% less, and the team bonus gives your Archers 2 extra line of sight, so they spot enemy Skirmishers and Scouts sooner.

The food trickle is slow. Do not cut sheep, boar or berry villagers further than this, or the Town Center will idle.

First 5 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop; the food trickle starts with the first wood drop off
Villager 9 goes to sheep
Villager 10 lures the first boar
Villager 11 builds a House, then a Mill at the berries, and forages there
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 in total)
Next 2 villagers on boar; lure the second boar when the first is about half eaten
Next 5 villagers to wood, with a second Lumber Camp when the first woodline gets crowded (8 on wood)
Research Loom while you finish collecting 500 food
Click up to the Feudal Age with 21 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, move 3 sheep or boar villagers to gold with a Mining Camp and 1 to wood
One wood villager builds a Barracks during the age up
Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build an Archery Range, then a second one right after
Make Archers from both ranges nonstop and keep them in one group
Research Double-Bit Axe, then Fletching when you have three or four Archers; the Shu pay 25% less for Fletching
New villagers go to wood and gold first, then to Farms as the food under the Town Center runs out
Research Horse Collar and Padded Archer Armor when you can afford them

after_feudal: Take the first six to eight Archers to the opponent's woodline or gold and stay in range of your own woodline when Scouts come. Keep Farms growing behind the army and add Wheelbarrow. Click up to the Castle Age with 15 to 20 Archers and research Crossbowman and Bodkin Arrow right away, both cheaper for the Shu. In the Castle Age, add Pikemen and later White Feather Guards as a front line, and consider a Siege Workshop for War Chariots or rams. Bolt Magazine in the Imperial Age is the payoff of the whole archer plan.
tips: Villagers 6 to 8 on wood is the Shu difference. Do not push it further; the trickle is slow.
Your Archers see 2 tiles further than normal. Use it to keep out of range of enemy Skirmishers and spot Scouts early.
Shu cavalry is weak, so a Spearman or two near your Archers is worth the food against Scout Cavalry.
Fletching and the Blacksmith archer armor are 25% cheaper, so research them earlier than you would with another civilization.
beaten_by: Skirmishers in numbers stop the archers; answer with Men-at-Arms or a few Scout Cavalry, or go up to the Castle Age quickly. Fast Scout Cavalry can kill villagers on gold before your archers are out, so wall the gold or keep the archers near it. Strong archer civilizations like the Britons win an even archer war in the Feudal Age; fight them near your towers until the Castle Age upgrades come in.

title: Shu Fast Castle War Chariots (27+2)
summary: Skip the Feudal fighting, reach the Castle Age with a Blacksmith ready and mass War Chariots from two or three Siege Workshops before the opponent has an answer.
description:
The War Chariot is a Shu Siege Workshop unit with cavalry armor, 6 range and two attack modes. Massed early in the Castle Age it shreds villagers, Archers and Spearmen, and it is quick enough to stay away from infantry. Red Phosphoru made the fast Castle version of this plan famous, and Hera's counter video called it a 62% win rate rush. The Viking Sagas patch then raised the chariot's cost to 75 food and 90 gold and its training time to 32 seconds. It is still a strong surprise, but it needs a clean economy now.

The Dark Age is a standard fast Castle build with one Shu change: the lumberjacks generate food, so you can run a little more wood and a little less berry food than usual. In the Feudal Age you need a Blacksmith anyway, because the Siege Workshop requires it, and one more Feudal building to click up.

The chariots cost food and gold only, so after the Castle Age lands, most new villagers go to gold. Plan for 10 or more gold miners to keep two Siege Workshops busy.

First 6 villagers on sheep under the Town Center
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop; the lumberjacks start adding food with every drop off
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill at the berries, and forages there
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 in total); lure the second boar when the first is about half eaten
Next 2 villagers on boar or sheep
When the sheep run low, move the most damaged sheep villagers onto Farms
Next 7 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (11 on wood)
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp and mine gold
Research Loom while you finish collecting 500 food
Click up to the Feudal Age with 27 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, one wood villager builds a Barracks; keep seeding Farms as the hunt runs out
Feudal Age arrives: build a Blacksmith (needed for the Siege Workshop) and an Archery Range
The 2 Feudal Age villagers go to gold (5 on gold)
Click up to the Castle Age as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold
While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar
Save 400 wood during the age up and build two Siege Workshops the moment the Castle Age arrives
New villagers go to gold; when the berries run out, move those villagers to gold as well
Make War Chariots nonstop from both workshops and attack once you have five or six; add a third workshop if the gold allows

after_feudal: Group the first five or six War Chariots and go for the opponent's woodline or gold. Use Barrage mode when the targets are spread out, such as villagers on a woodline or a loose group of Archers, and Focus Fire against a tight line of units or a single tough target. The land siege speed bonus makes the chariots easier to pull back when cavalry comes. Keep the Town Center making villagers, move most of them to gold, and add Farms. Once the raid has done its damage, build a Castle for White Feather Guards to guard the chariots, or a third Town Center to turn the lead into economy. If the opponent answers with Knights or Camel Riders, add Pikemen and White Feather Guards in front of the chariots instead of chasing.
tips: The Siege Workshop needs a Blacksmith, so the Blacksmith is one of your two Feudal buildings.
Do not trickle chariots in one or two at a time; they work in groups.
War Chariots cost no wood. After the workshops are up, you can move some lumberjacks to Farms and gold.
Wall your woodline before clicking to the Castle Age; the build has no army in the Feudal Age.
Against a walled opponent, the chariots still kill anything near the walls, but bring a ram or two for the gates.
beaten_by: Fast melee cavalry such as Knights or Camel Riders catches War Chariots before they mass, and a well timed Feudal rush hurts the build before the chariots exist. Strong Mangonel or Onager play also punishes clumped chariots. Against those answers, add White Feather Guards or Pikemen and switch the second workshop to rams, or go back to Crossbowmen.

title: Sicilians Donjon Rush (21 pop)
summary: Build a Donjon next to the enemy woodline or gold with your starting stone, train Serjeants from it and let them build more Donjons, so the push runs without pulling more villagers away from home.
description:
The Donjon is the Sicilian tower. It costs 50 wood and 175 stone, and Sicilians start with 300 stone, so the first one needs no stone mining. You can place it during the Dark Age, and it starts shooting once you reach the Feudal Age. It trains Serjeants, armored infantry that can build further Donjons, so after the first Donjon your villagers can go home while Serjeants carry on.

You play a normal Dark Age into a 21 population click, with two villagers on gold for the Serjeants and Loom. During the age up three villagers walk forward and build the first Donjon next to the enemy woodline or gold, timed to finish when Feudal Age arrives. Two more villagers mine stone at home so a second Donjon follows within a couple of minutes.

Pick it on open maps like Arabia, where the woodline and gold sit away from the enemy Town Center. Serjeants in the Feudal Age are similar to a sturdier Man-at-Arms, and they become strong main infantry with the free upgrade when you reach the Castle Age. Video guides use 20 to 21 villagers for this build.

First 6 villagers on sheep
Next 3 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop wood
Villager 10 lures the first boar
Villager 11 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries
Next 3 villagers on berries (4 on berries)
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar; lure the second boar
Next 2 villagers go to wood (5 on wood)
Next 2 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold and mine
Research Loom
Click up to the Feudal Age with 20 villagers plus the scout
Right after the click, 3 sheep villagers walk forward and build the first Donjon (50 wood, 175 stone) next to the enemy woodline or gold
Move 2 food villagers to stone and build a Mining Camp; you need 50 more stone for the second Donjon
Feudal Age arrives: the Donjon starts shooting; train Serjeants from it nonstop
New villagers go to food and start Farms; research Horse Collar early, since Sicilian farm upgrades give extra food
With 175 stone, the forward villagers or the first Serjeants build a second Donjon closer to the enemy gold or main woodline
Send the forward villagers home to wood once two Donjons stand; Serjeants do the building from now on
Next 2 villagers go to gold (4 on gold) to keep Serjeants coming
When the opponent is pinned, click up to the Castle Age; Serjeants upgrade for free when it arrives

after_feudal: Keep at least one Donjon making Serjeants and use the Serjeants to repair Donjons under attack, block enemy villagers and kill builders. If the opponent abandons the woodline or gold, keep stepping Donjons toward the next resource. Click Castle Age once the enemy is falling behind. In Castle Age the Serjeants gain hit points, attack and armor for free; add a Town Center or two (Sicilian Town Centers build twice as fast), and go Knights or more Serjeants depending on what the opponent makes.
tips: Serjeants build 25 percent slower than villagers, so bring the villagers for the first Donjon and let Serjeants handle the next ones.
Keep 50 wood with every 175 stone; a Donjon needs both.
Garrison a Serjeant or villager in a Donjon under attack only in Castle Age; in Feudal Age garrisoned units add no arrows.
Donjons can also train Spearmen, so you can answer Scout Cavalry from the front.
Watch for a fake tower: an opponent may start a tower near your Donjon spot and cancel it once you commit.
beaten_by: Fast reactions break it: villagers pulled to attack the Donjon before it finishes, a forward Barracks with Men-at-Arms or Spearmen to kill the builders, and walls that close the targeted resource. Archers outrange Feudal Donjons and kill Serjeants that leave them. A player who moves to another woodline and goes for a fast Castle Age with Mangonels or Knights can make your stone investment look poor, so watch for that and switch to a boom in time.

summary: A 19 pop Scout Cavalry opening where a home Donjon from your starting stone replaces the Barracks, unlocks the Stable and guards your berries, and your scouts take much less damage from Spearmen.
description:
For the Sicilians, a Donjon unlocks the Stable and Archery Range in place of a Barracks. A Donjon costs 50 wood and 175 stone, and the Sicilians start with 300 stone, so you can build one at home during the age up and save 125 wood compared with a Barracks. The Donjon shoots from the Feudal Age and can train Spearmen, which gives you a defense against an opposing scout or Men-at-Arms rush at your berries or Farms.

The scouts themselves are better than usual: Sicilian units take 40 percent less bonus damage, so enemy Spearmen hurt your Scout Cavalry much less. You can fight through a couple of Spearmen that would stop other civilizations' scouts.

Use it on open maps for map control and to slow the opponent's Feudal Age. The common follow up is Knights in Castle Age, which also benefit from the bonus damage reduction, and a fast extra Town Center since yours build twice as fast in Castle Age.

Keep adding Farms; build a Blacksmith with a wood villager
Put 3 more villagers on gold (6 on gold) to get ready for Castle Age Knights
Click up to the Castle Age with 800 food and 200 gold

after_feudal: Raid with the scouts, kill the enemy scout and stay in fights against a few Spearmen longer than other civilizations could. Train a couple of Spearmen from the Donjon if the opponent sends their own scouts at your Farms. In Castle Age, build a second Stable for Knights and drop a second Town Center behind them; it finishes twice as fast as normal. Heavy Plow is worth an early click for you because of the farm bonus.
tips: Do not build a Barracks at all in the Feudal Age; the Donjon covers the Stable requirement.
Place the Donjon so it covers your berries and part of your future Farms.
Your scouts lose less to Spearmen, but large numbers of Spearmen with villagers still win; retreat when you see five or more.
If you need stone later for a second Donjon or a Castle, put two villagers on stone after the Stable is up.
beaten_by: Walls and towers stop scouts regardless of the bonus, and a Men-at-Arms into archers opening trades well against Scout Cavalry. Archers behind walls are the hardest answer. When the opponent turtles, go home and take a faster Castle Age with an extra Town Center, or switch the Stable production to Light Cavalry and the Archery Range to Skirmishers.

Hera plays this with two Stables and Bloodlines in the Feudal Age, then a one Town Center push in the Castle Age with Knights and a Siege Workshop. Mangonels and rams cost 15% less for the Slavs, so the push hits earlier and keeps going longer.

title: Tatars Fast Castle into Cavalry Archers (25+2)

title: Turks Fast Imperial (29+2+2)
summary: A one Town Center race to the Imperial Age, landing around 19 to 20 minutes. Free Chemistry lets you train Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons the moment you arrive, and the Turk gold mining bonus pays for both age ups.
description:
The Turks are one of the few civilizations where a fast Imperial Age works as a 1v1 plan. Their gold miners work 25% faster, which matters because the Castle and Imperial ages cost 200 and 800 gold. Chemistry is free, so the gunpowder units are ready the moment the age lands, and those units have 25% more HP and train 25% faster.

You click Feudal at 29 pop, spend only the minimum time in Feudal and Castle Age, and stay on one Town Center. While the Imperial Age loads you build a Barracks and two Archery Ranges. Then you push with Hand Cannoneers and two or three Bombard Cannons against an opponent who is usually still booming with few units.

The build punishes greedy booms on Arena and other closed maps. An experienced opponent can see it coming and counter it with Crossbowmen and Ballistics or with upgraded Knights, so scout and adjust.

title: Turks Scouts (19 pop)
summary: A standard 19 pop Scout Cavalry opening where your scouts have +1 pierce armor, which makes them much harder for archers to kill. It leads into a Castle Age with free Light Cavalry and fast gold mining.
description:
Scout Cavalry is the unit Turk players make most on the ladder, and the reason is the extra pierce armor. With Scale Barding Armor, Turkish scouts take very little damage from Feudal archers, so the usual archer defense against scouts works poorly. The Turks have no other Dark Age bonus, so the Dark Age is a normal 19 pop scout build.

In the Feudal Age you raid with the scouts while your gold miners, who work 25% faster, prepare the Castle Age. In the Castle Age the Light Cavalry upgrade is free, so your surviving scouts become Light Cavalry without spending anything, and the Hussar upgrade is free later too.

From there you can go Knights, Camel Riders or cavalry archers, depending on what you scouted. The scouts are a good way to protect the Turks' slow early game.

Raid with the scouts in one group. Thanks to the extra pierce armor you can fight through a few archers or a tower's arrows for longer than other civilizations, but still run from Spearmen and Camel Riders.

In the Castle Age your scouts become Light Cavalry for free. Use them to hunt Monks and raid while you add a second Town Center. Then choose the main unit: Knights against archers and infantry, Camel Riders against Knights, or cavalry archers with Sipahi if you have a lot of gold. Take a second gold mine before the first runs low and keep the gold miners busy; the Turk economy runs on gold.

title: Varangians Bloodlines Scouts (20 pop)
summary: A beginner friendly scout rush that turns the Varangian hunt gold into an early Bloodlines, giving your Scout Cavalry 75 hit points before the opponent's scouts have upgrades.
description:
Varangian shepherds and hunters drop off 10% extra gold with their food, and Bloodlines gives Varangian mounted units 30 hit points instead of 20. Put together, that is the whole idea of this build. By the time the sheep and boars are eaten you have collected enough gold for Bloodlines without sending anyone to a gold mine, and Scout Cavalry with 75 hit points win almost every Feudal Age fight against other scouts and take far longer to kill with Spearmen or towers.

The Dark Age is a plain 20 population scout opening with no deer pushing, so it works on maps with deer or chickens alike. Keep the food on sheep and boars as long as possible, since those are the sources that pay gold. Berries and Farms do not.

This is a good first build for new players: the timings are forgiving, the scouts are hard to lose, and the follow-up into Knights uses the same Stable and the same upgrade.

With 75 hit points they can fight enemy scouts head on and survive a few Spearman hits, but they still lose a long fight against groups of Spearmen, so raid where the pikes are not. Keep villager production going, grow to 15 or more Farms and put 6 to 8 villagers on gold. Click the Castle Age once you have six to eight scouts and the economy upgrades. In the Castle Age the scouts become Light Cavalry and your Knights start with 130 hit points, so Knights from one or two Stables are the natural follow-up.
