Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar
Next 6 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (10 on wood); move shepherds to Farms as the sheep run out
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp and mine gold
Research Loom and click up to the Feudal Age with 27 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
During the age up, keep seeding Farms and wall your woodlines with Houses and palisades
Feudal Age arrives: 2 wood villagers build a Blacksmith and a Market (or a Stable if you plan Hei Guang Cavalry)
Research Double-Bit Axe; it gives you a free villager, send it to gold
Research Horse Collar; the free villager goes to Farms
Click up to the Castle Age with 800 food and 200 gold
While the age loads, research Gold Mining for one more free villager; add a few villagers to stone if you want a Castle
Castle Age arrives: build 2 more Town Centers with wood villagers
Research Wheelbarrow and Bow Saw, then Heavy Plow and Hand Cart; each one adds a free villager
Build an Archery Range for Xianbei Raiders or a Stable for Hei Guang Cavalry, depending on what you scout
Build a Castle once you have 650 stone for Tiger Cavalry and Tuntian

after_feudal:
The Castle Age is where the build pays off. Keep all three Town Centers producing and research every economy upgrade the moment you can afford it, including Stone Mining and Gold Shaft Mining. Aim for 70 to 80 villagers before you commit to a big attack.

While the boom runs, defend with a small army of the right type: Xianbei Raiders against infantry pushes, Spearmen and a few Hei Guang Cavalry against scouts and Knights. Once the economy is up, mass Xianbei Raiders with Hei Guang or Tiger Cavalry and attack, adding Tuntian when the army reaches 25 or more units.
tips: Each free villager appears at your Town Center; give it a job right away or set a rally point to a resource.
Feudal Wheelbarrow keeps the Town Center busy for a long time; most players take it early in the Castle Age instead.
On water maps, Gillnets at the Dock also gives a free villager.
Wall before you click up; the Wei have nothing to stop a Feudal rush except the free villagers.
Scout the opponent's army before you pick Tiger Cavalry, Xianbei Raiders or Hei Guang Cavalry; each has a clear job.
beaten_by: A strong Feudal rush before your walls are up is the main problem. Archers on your woodline or scouts on your Farms force you to make Skirmishers or Spearmen and delay the Castle Age. In the Castle Age, opponents who attack the new Town Centers with Knights or a forward Castle before your army is out can stop the boom; keep a few Spearmen and Hei Guang Cavalry at home and garrison the Town Centers when needed.

title: Wu Fast Castle into Jian Swordsmen (27+2)
summary: A Fast Castle that picks Feudal buildings which pay food back, then trains Jian Swordsmen from three Barracks to walk through an archer army in the early Castle Age.
description:
Jian Swordsmen carry 5 pierce armor while shielded and bonus damage against archers. In the early Castle Age, Crossbowmen barely hurt them, and Wu regeneration gets damaged Jian back over the 45 hit point line so their shields come back. Hera made two 2025 videos about this Jian Swordsman rush, and it is at its best against archer civilizations and opponents who boom behind Crossbowmen.

The build is a normal 27+2 fast Castle with Wu details. One villager builds the starting Houses. You need two Feudal Age buildings to click up, and instead of a Market you build an Archery Range or Stable next to the Blacksmith, which gives 55 food. In the Castle Age, two more Barracks give another 110 food, so three Barracks start producing almost for free in food terms.

Jian Swordsmen cost 45 food and 50 gold and take a while to train, so gold miners decide how many you get. Send most new villagers to gold during the Castle Age research.

steps.text: One starting villager builds both Houses; the other two go to the sheep; scout for more sheep
Next villagers on sheep until 6 are on food
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries, and gathers there
Next 4 villagers on berries (5 on berries); lure the second boar
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar; sheep villagers start Farms as sheep run out
Next 5 villagers build a second Lumber Camp and chop (9 on wood)
One of them builds a Barracks; it gives 55 food when it finishes
Next 3 villagers build a Mining Camp on gold
Research Loom while you finish the 500 food
Click up to the Feudal Age with 26 villagers plus the Scout Cavalry
Feudal Age arrives: two wood villagers build a Blacksmith and an Archery Range or Stable; the range or Stable gives 55 food
Next 2 villagers go to gold (5 on gold)
Click up to the Castle Age as soon as you have 800 food and 200 gold
While the age loads, research Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar
New villagers go to gold until about 10 are mining; move berry villagers to gold and Farms when the berries run out
Before the Castle Age arrives, two wood villagers start two more Barracks; each one gives 55 food
Castle Age arrives at about 16 minutes; start Jian Swordsmen from all three Barracks
Research Scale Mail Armor and Forging at the Blacksmith once production is running

after_feudal: Move out with eight to ten Jian Swordsmen and a few Pikemen in case of Knights. Aim for the archers and the villagers behind them, and pull back badly damaged Jian so regeneration can restore their shields. Add Chain Mail Armor, Squires and a second Town Center while the push is going. If the opponent answers with Knights or Long Swordsmen, switch the Barracks to Pikemen or Long Swordsmen. Fire Archers from a Castle help break towers and walls, since your Siege Workshop has no Capped Ram.
tips: Pick the Feudal buildings that pay food: Barracks, Archery Range, Stable and Dock all give 55 food, the Market and Blacksmith do not.
Jian Swordsmen regain their shield when they heal past 45 hit points. Rotate damaged ones out of the fight.
Against Knights, Jian Swordsmen lose. Keep Pikemen in the group.
Wall before you click up to the Castle Age; you have almost no army in the Feudal Age.
beaten_by: Knights, Long Swordsmen and Samurai beat Jian Swordsmen in melee, so scout what the opponent makes in the Castle Age and change unit if needed. Mangonels hit clumped infantry hard; spread the Jian before they walk into range. A Feudal rush before your walls are up hurts as with every fast Castle; keep the Barracks ready for Spearmen and use Houses, which you build quickly, to wall.

title: Wu Men-at-Arms into Archers (25 pop)
summary: Three militia made in the Dark Age become regenerating Men-at-Arms in the Feudal Age, while the food from the Barracks and the Archery Range helps you set up a range of Fletching archers behind them.
description:
The standard Men-at-Arms opening fits the Wu well. The Dark Age Barracks gives 55 food when it finishes, which covers most of the cost of one militia. In the Feudal Age, Wu infantry regenerate 10 hit points per minute, so Men-at-Arms that pull back after a fight are healthy again for the next one. The Archery Range you build next pays another 55 food.

The opening also uses the fast Houses. One starting villager builds both Houses while the other two go to the sheep right away, which gives you a small head start on food.

The three militia use the starting gold, so there are no gold miners before the Feudal Age. You click up with 21 villagers, three militia and the scout, which makes 25 pop. Once the Men-at-Arms are out, an Archery Range and a Blacksmith go up at home.

steps.text: One starting villager builds both Houses; the other two go to the sheep; scout for more sheep
Next villagers on sheep until 6 are on food
Next 4 villagers build a Lumber Camp and chop
Villager 11 lures the first boar
Villager 12 builds a House, then a Mill on the berries, and gathers there
Next 2 villagers on berries (3 on berries)
Villager 15 builds a Barracks next to the woodline; it gives 55 food when it finishes, then this villager chops
Train three Militia from the Barracks with the starting gold, then send them towards the enemy woodline
Next 2 villagers on sheep and boar; lure the second boar
Next 4 villagers chop wood (9 on wood)
Click up to the Feudal Age with 21 villagers, three Militia and the scout; skip Loom
During the age up, move 3 food villagers to build a Mining Camp on gold
Feudal Age arrives: research the Man-at-Arms upgrade right away and keep the Militia near the enemy woodline until it finishes
Two wood villagers build an Archery Range (another 55 food) and a Blacksmith
Research Double-Bit Axe
Next 4 villagers to gold (7 on gold)
Start Archers from the range and research Fletching once the first few are out
New villagers go to Farms as sheep and boar run out, and to wood; research Horse Collar

after_feudal: Use the Men-at-Arms to chase villagers off wood, gold and berries, and pull them back when they drop low; regeneration brings them back for a second round. Once the archers have Fletching, push together with the Men-at-Arms in front. Add Scale Mail Armor if the opponent fights with Archers. Click up to the Castle Age at about 28 to 30 villagers, and pick Jian Swordsmen if the opponent went archers or Hei Guang Cavalry if they went Skirmishers. Every new Barracks or Stable you build in the Castle Age pays 55 food.
tips: Build both starting Houses with a single villager. Wu Houses go up twice as fast.
Do not fight to the last hit point. Retreat damaged Men-at-Arms and let them regenerate.
A second Barracks in the Feudal Age costs 175 wood but gives 55 food back, so it is cheap if you want more infantry.
Against an opponent who walls quickly, use the Men-at-Arms to guard your own woodline and switch to a faster Castle Age.
beaten_by: Early walls and Archers stop Men-at-Arms. If the opponent has Archers out first, keep your infantry home and add Skirmishers from your range. A Scout Cavalry opening is fine as long as you have a Spearman or two. Towers next to your woodline are awkward for Men-at-Arms; answer with villagers and your own Archers.
